Vulnerabilities & Patching.title: Microsoft’s AI bug hunter finds Rust flaw that went undetected for nearly 11 years
Vulnerabilities & Patching.context: Microsoft said the researchers found no reliable exploitation path under the conditions they examined and assessed practical exploitation as unlikely
Vulnerabilities & Patching.full_text:
Microsoft researchers have uncovered a memory-safety bug in Rust’s standard library that had gone undetected for nearly 11 years, alongside other flaws that can trigger undefined behavior even in applications written entirely in safe Rust. Two of the findings affect stable Rust, including a separate issue that could cause applications to access freed memory.

The nearly 11-year-old bug involves Rust’s process::exit function. Microsoft’s FORGE Lab researchers found that calling the function from a child thread could cause the runtime to remove the main thread’s alternate signal stack while it was still running. If the main thread subsequently experienced a stack overflow, the operating system could be unable to deliver the signal correctly, resulting in a segmentation fault instead of Rust’s intended stack-overflow handling.

“The process::exit signal stack bug was in the standard library for nearly 11 years,” the researchers wrote in a blog post. Microsoft said the researchers found no reliable exploitation path under the conditions they examined and assessed practical exploitation as unlikely.

The research used Hyenas, FORGE Lab’s AI-powered vulnerability-scanning system, to investigate unsafe code in Rust’s standard library. Hyenas is the lab’s research version of codename MDASH, Microsoft’s agentic vulnerability-discovery system.

Microsoft said some of the bugs were found with help from Hyenas. Researchers then examined the underlying code, reproduced the issues, assessed their security impact, and reported them to Rust maintainers.

Microsoft said the practical risk is limited. Each flaw requires unusual conditions to trigger, and a bug in the standard library becomes “a serious vulnerability only if a real program reaches the API in that way,” the researchers wrote.

Unsafe code challenges Rust’s safety guarantees

Rust’s ownership model and type system are designed to prevent memory-safety problems commonly associated with languages such as C and C++. However, its standard library relies on unsafe code internally for operations that the compiler cannot verify.

Components such as Vec and String use these operations but expose them through safe APIs. Microsoft said these APIs must meet a strict soundness requirement: “no matter how safe code uses it, it must be impossible to trigger undefined behavior.”

Microsoft grouped the findings into three categories: unsafe code that assumes operations will not panic, code that trusts user-provided implementations to behave correctly, and code that makes incorrect assumptions about the underlying system.

The first involved a panic-safety problem in Rust’s MapWindows::clone implementation. The function created a buffer before fully initializing its contents and then called a user-provided clone operation to populate it. If that operation triggered a panic, Rust’s unwinding mechanism could invoke the buffer’s destructor, which would attempt to access uninitialized memory. Microsoft said the reported fix prevents the partially initialized buffer from being destroyed before initialization is complete.

Another finding involved str::replace. The researchers found that the function could make an incorrect assumption about a custom implementation of the nightly Pattern trait. A custom implementation could supply a non-ASCII byte where the code expected an ASCII character, causing the replacement operation to produce invalid UTF-8 data. Subsequent string operations could then trigger undefined behavior, Microsoft said.

System-level bugs affect stable Rust

Microsoft said the first two categories of weaknesses were already being studied in 2021 through Rudra, a static analyzer developed by members of the research team. The standard library had also addressed panic-safety problems as far back as 2015, but similar weaknesses continue to appear in its implementations.

The third category involves interactions between Rust and underlying operating systems and C libraries. Besides the process::exit issue, researchers identified a problem in Rust’s CommandExt::exec functionality involving the process-wide environment variable array.

Microsoft found that the function could modify this shared state while holding a read lock, potentially allowing other threads to access inconsistent data. Under certain conditions, concurrent operations could leave the environment pointer referencing freed memory.

Microsoft said both the process::exit and CommandExt::exec findings affect stable Rust. A proposed fix for the environment-variable issue, which avoids modifying the shared array by calling execve directly, was under review when the blog was published.

Two issues reported by Microsoft’s team remained open at publication. The blog also discussed related reports from other researchers and fixes still under review.

Findings feed into Microsoft’s security products

Microsoft said the research findings can also feed into Microsoft Perception, its multi-agent security system, where specialized agents work across broader security workflows. It would therefore help the company improve the development of MDASH, which brings agentic vulnerability discovery into Microsoft Defender.

For example, Microsoft’s Web App Pen Test Agent can use MDASH findings to prioritize testing, assess exploitability against live applications, and provide information to support remediation, the researchers wrote.

“Our goal isn’t to simply find more bugs,” the researchers wrote, but to identify meaningful issues and improve the safety of foundational software developers and organizations depend on. The Rust project had not responded to a request for comment from CSO at the time of writing.

Vulnerabilities & Patching.title: Binance Warns of iOS Sandbox Escape That Could Expose Crypto Wallet Keys, No Fix Confirmed
Vulnerabilities & Patching.context: Apple's updates for iOS 26 and 27, released yesterday, do not list a fix
Vulnerabilities & Patching.full_text:
An iOS sandbox escape published on GitHub lets an app read other apps' files on iPhones running iOS 26 and 27. That puts seed phrases, private keys, and login credentials at risk of exposure to malicious apps, Binance warned today. Apple's updates for iOS 26 and 27, released yesterday, do not list a fix.

A researcher who goes by forcequit released the escape, called worse_query, on Sunday, a day before those updates came out. Neither the exchange nor the researcher reported any attacks or thefts involving it.

The exchange told users to delete apps installed from untrusted sources, such as sideloaded or manually signed apps, and to update iOS and all their apps. No fix for the escape has been confirmed.

For anyone who suspects a breach, the exchange's security warning advises moving funds to a new wallet created on a clean device and resetting all active login sessions.

The researcher's proof-of-concept code can reach every app's data container on an iPhone, and some system folders on iOS 27. To use it, an app has to set up an App Group container.

He says the code is for developers and "isn't useful by itself." Other developers have built apps on it that people can install.

One of them is WQ Files, a file manager that developer Christoph Kolbicz built on worse_query. It reaches other apps' data without a jailbreak or a kernel exploit, and it can edit, delete and clear that data.

WQ Files installs via sideloading tools such as AltStore and SideStore, which automatically create the App Group it needs when used with an Apple ID. No one involved has said whether an app from the App Store could use worse_query.

The three versions in the exchange's warning are the ones listed as tested in the WQ Files release notes. The researcher gives a wider range.

Of these sources, only Erosion's developers list iOS 27.2.1, which came out yesterday, and none lists iOS 26.7.3. They added 27.2.1 this week in a README change with the note "pretty sure 27.2.1 is supported".

Yesterday's updates, iOS 27.2.1 and iOS 26.7.3, fixed two iMessage flaws and several Bluetooth bugs. The security notes for iOS 27.2.1 do not mention worse_query or any sandbox issues, nor do the iOS 26.7.3 notes. Apple does not disclose, discuss, or confirm security issues until it has investigated and a patch or release is available, the notes say.

In a reply on X, the researcher wrote that he had not planned to release worse_query early. He added that "Apple was stalling on responding to me and people started larping with it on here."

The exchange did not name any wallet app as exposed, and neither did the researcher nor the developers of the apps built on worse_query.

Vulnerabilities & Patching.title: CISA Adds Six Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
Vulnerabilities & Patching.context: While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog...
Vulnerabilities & Patching.full_text:
CISA has added six new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog, based on evidence of active exploitation.

CVE-2026-20320 Cisco BroadWorks Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference Vulnerability

CVE-2026-111560 Barracuda Networks Multiple Products OS Command Injection Vulnerability

CVE-2026-111793 Openwave Messaging Limited Webtop Media Transcoder Incorrect Resource Transfer Between Spheres Vulnerability

CVE-2026-116606 Barracuda Networks Email Security Gateway (ESG) Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel Vulnerability

CVE-2026-124194 Microsoft Office Outlook Missing User Interaction for Potentially Unsafe Action Vulnerability

CVE-2026-125350 Google Chromium Use-After-Free Vulnerability

These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise.

Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied.

While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities. CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria.

Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form. Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance.

Vulnerabilities & Patching.title: Apple Patches iMessage Group Chat Privacy Flaws and Bluetooth Pairing Vulnerabilities
Vulnerabilities & Patching.context: An iMessage flaw could let a remote attacker join a group chat and receive its messages, Apple said yesterday, and it released updates to fix it
Vulnerabilities & Patching.full_text:
An iMessage flaw could let a remote attacker join a group chat and receive its messages, Apple said yesterday, and it released updates to fix it. The updates also fix a separate iMessage flaw that could let someone added to a group access messages sent before they joined.

As of today, other updates released yesterday for the iPhone XS, XS Max and XR, the iPad (7th generation) and some Apple Watch models do not list either fix.

The company's notes also do not say whether either flaw has been exploited, what an attacker would need, whether group members would see someone who joined this way, or whether every member must update to be protected.

The updates that fix the iMessage flaws also fix a flaw in Google's Brotli compression library. The notes do not mention any attacks using that flaw. The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 27.

The flaw that could let a remote attacker join a group chat is tracked as CVE-2026-113961. It is an authorization issue that the updates fix through improved validation. The flaw involving earlier messages is CVE-2026-113960.

Which Updates Carry the Fixes

Each operating system version got its own update. The security advisory for iOS and iPadOS 27.2.1 describes all three flaws. The security releases list links to the notes for every update.

The iOS 18.7.12 notes and the watchOS 26.6.1 notes list other security fixes but not the iMessage or Brotli fixes.

The company does not say whether devices on those versions are affected by the three flaws. Its notes also offer no workaround for anyone who cannot update right away.

The Brotli flaw, CVE-2026-111497, is an out-of-bounds write in the library's decoder that could let malicious input corrupt memory. CISA's catalog entry for the Brotli decoder flaw names Google's Brotli as the affected product and says different products could use the component.

All nine updates fix Bluetooth and AirPlay flaws. Two could allow a malicious Bluetooth device, or an attacker within Bluetooth range, to pair with a device without user interaction. The notes do not say what a paired device could then do.

Two others could let an attacker bypass the limit on pairing code attempts, one from Bluetooth range and one from the same network. Another could let an attacker in Bluetooth range corrupt process memory.

Vulnerabilities & Patching.title: SAP Patches Four CVSS 10.0 Flaws, Including Two Enabling Remote Code Execution
Vulnerabilities & Patching.context: Four flaws that attackers could exploit without logging in were fixed today as part of SAP's monthly Security Patch Day—the vendor rates all four 10
Vulnerabilities & Patching.full_text:
Four flaws that attackers could exploit without logging in were fixed today as part of SAP's monthly Security Patch Day—the vendor rates all four 10.0, the maximum CVSS score.

Three are in the SAP NetWeaver application server, the software SAP systems run on, and one is in the Web Dispatcher, which receives web requests from the internet and passes them on to that server.

The flaws in the Web Dispatcher and the Internet Communication Manager (ICM), which handles the server's web traffic, could allow an attacker who can reach the software over the network to run code, the vendor says.

The flaw in the server's SAML 2.0 service provider, which hands off user sign-in to an identity provider, could allow an attacker to log in as any user on some systems that use SAML single sign-on.

The flaw in SAP Gateway, which connects the server to other SAP systems and programs, could allow an attacker to impersonate one of the system's own servers and take unauthorized actions.

None of the four require any user action to work.

Affected Versions and SAP Notes

Each flaw is fixed in its own note, and the affected versions differ by component, according to SAP's November security bulletin. The notes are in SAP for Me, which requires a sign-in, and the vendor strongly recommends applying them as a priority.

SAP_BASIS 702, 731, 740, 750, 751, 752, 753, 754, 755, 756, 757, 758, 816, 920, 921, 922

Kernels that are out of maintenance are affected too, according to Onapsis, an SAP security company whose researchers found the ICM, Web Dispatcher and Gateway flaws. Its ICM2SHELL advisory lists kernels 7.40, 7.41, 7.42, 7.45, 7.49, 7.73, 7.81, 7.85 and 7.89 for the ICM and Web Dispatcher flaws, and its PROXYGATE advisory lists the same kernels plus 7.20 and 7.21 for the Gateway flaw. These kernels may not get a fix and need an upgrade to one that is still maintained.

What Each Flaw Allows

On the affected SAML setups, an attacker could use CVE-2026-120017 to log in as privileged users too, according to the vendor. A full compromise could follow, possibly reaching connected systems.

A different SAML flaw in the same software, CVE-2026-44748, was fixed on June 9 and needed an attacker with a normal user account.

In the ICM flaw (CVE-2026-76964) and the Web Dispatcher flaw (CVE-2026-89126), crafted network traffic could corrupt memory. An attacker who succeeds could then run code and fully compromise the system.

Onapsis says both flaws come from one bug, which it calls ICM2SHELL, in kernel code the ICM and Web Dispatcher share for putting split WebSocket messages back together. It gave the vendor a working exploit that runs operating system commands as <sid>adm, the account that owns the SAP installation.

The same bug can crash either component, and a crashed Web Dispatcher cuts off every SAP system behind it while it restarts. WebSocket support is on by default, so a system is exposed even if nothing uses it, and dual-stack systems are affected through their ABAP stack. The company's researchers have not seen the bug exploited in attacks.

SAP Gateway uses access control lists to decide which outside programs may connect to it, which programs it may start and which connections it may relay for others. In CVE-2026-89103, the gateway enables its default list with high privileges, allowing an external attacker to be treated as one of the system's own application servers. That attacker could then take unauthorized actions in the application environment.

The researchers who found the flaw call it PROXYGATE. They say exposure depends on the gateway's proxy list, prxyinfo, or on a profile parameter where that list is missing, not on the secinfo and reginfo lists that most hardening guidance covers. Where the proxy settings allow it, crafted requests make the gateway treat an outside attacker as one of its own application servers, and it could then run operating system commands for the attacker as <sid>adm.

The flaw affects any system that runs a gateway, including AS Java, dual-stack and standalone gateway installations. The researchers demonstrated the attack end to end in a proof of concept shared with the vendor, and they have not seen it exploited in attacks.

What to Do

In its Patch Day analysis, RedRays, a company that reviewed the notes in SAP for Me today, advises updating the kernel and all Web Dispatchers in a single rollout. That rollout should reach levels that cover all 17 of this month's kernel and Web Dispatcher fixes.

The firm's guidance for each flaw, except where another source is named:

SAML2 (CVE-2026-120017). Under certain configurations, the service provider did not check signatures on incoming assertions. Treat any AS ABAP system that uses SAML2 for browser logon, such as Fiori Launchpad or Web GUI behind an identity provider, as in scope until shown otherwise. There is no workaround, so the correction instructions or the listed support package are the only fix. The firm's SAML2 analysis also suggests reviewing every trusted identity provider in transaction SAML2 and checking audit logs for SAML logons by privileged users from unexpected sources.

SAP Gateway (CVE-2026-89103). Onapsis advises checking the proxy list, prxyinfo, first. A permissive one, open to broad networks or any host, leaves a system exposed at any patch level, so restrict it, starting with gateways that can be reached from the internet. Where there is no prxyinfo file, the profile parameter gw/acl_mode_proxy decides, and it ships set to 0, which allows every proxy connection. Kernels 7.93 and 9.16 already have the parameter and need it set to 1, kernels 7.22, 7.53, 7.54, 7.77 and 8.04 gain it with the kernel patch, and 9.20 and 9.21 also get a kernel patch. The kernel patch alone, without a restrictive prxyinfo or gw/acl_mode_proxy set to 1, does not take a system out of scope. There is no official workaround, but a restrictive prxyinfo reduces exposure until the patch is in, and the firm also advises limiting the gateway ports (33NN and 48NN) to hosts that need RFC access.

ICM (CVE-2026-76964). WebSocket control frames with invalid length fields cause a heap out-of-bounds write before any login. SAP NetWeaver AS Java is not affected, and the fix ships through dw.sar and the SP Stack Kernel. If users reach the ICM only through a Web Dispatcher, patching that Web Dispatcher to the levels in FAQ note 3778788 shields the ICM for now, according to RedRays' ICM analysis. That holds only if nobody can reach the ICM ports directly. The ICM2SHELL advisory adds that the shield does not work on a Web Dispatcher set up as a router (PROT=ROUTER). It also warns that on release 7.93 a higher patch level is not always a fixed one: patch level 419 is still vulnerable, and only the updated 401 Stack Kernel, 402 once released, and 420 or later carry the fix. Turning off WebSocket support blocks the bug as a last resort, but it breaks features that depend on it.

Web Dispatcher (CVE-2026-89126). It has the same root cause as the ICM flaw. It affects standalone and embedded Web Dispatchers, including those in SAP HANA XS Classic and XS Advanced, but not SAP Content Server. The firm's Web Dispatcher analysis lists the patch paths: SAPWEBDISP.SAR for standalone instances, dw.sar or the SP Stack Kernel for embedded ones, SPS08 revision 089.05 or SPS07 revision 079.11 for HANA XS Classic, and version 1.5.4 or later for XS Advanced. Turning off WebSocket support works until the patch is in, but the note warns that this affects ABAP Push Channels and some Fiori features. Find every Web Dispatcher first, because one missed instance leaves the flaw open.

(The story was updated after publication on November 10, 2026, to include details from the researchers who found the ICM, Web Dispatcher and Gateway flaws.)

Corrected on November 10, 2026: an earlier version tied the SAP Gateway flaw to the secinfo and reginfo lists and said kernels from 7.93 on already have the gw/acl_mode_proxy parameter, but the researchers who found the flaw say the proxy list, prxyinfo, or that parameter decides exposure, and kernel 8.04 gets the parameter only with the patch.

Vulnerabilities & Patching.title: Security Flaws Across UK Government Sites Exposed ‘God-Tier’ Information
Vulnerabilities & Patching.context: A security researcher has found more than 100 serious vulnerabilities in publicly available UK government code, putting sensitive data at risk as a result of poor cyber hygiene
Vulnerabilities & Patching.full_text:
A security researcher has found more than 100 serious vulnerabilities in publicly available UK government code, putting sensitive data at risk as a result of poor cyber hygiene.

The UK government has defaulted to openly publishing code it produces with public money for around a decade because it’s transparent, and making it easier for code to be reused is cost-efficient. This includes within the Department of Health and Social Care, and the Home Office, as well as local authorities.

But funding squeezes have left departments neglecting maintenance and improvement of their technology estate. While ControlPlane security researcher Chris Nesbitt-Smith found the vulnerabilities using Claude’s Opus and Sonnet AI models, he says that he used consumer-grade models on a laptop and that many of the issues could have been caught by a routine IT health check. “None of this is the level of sophistication that general media is worried about in terms of cyber attacks,” he tells WIRED. “It’s all daft stuff.”

In the most serious case he identified, the Planning Inspectorate, which handles land-use matters across England, had failed to fully remove a login after it accidentally committed them to public repository GitHub. The fact the credentials gave such wide access—and seemingly didn’t expire—compounded with the agency’s accidental publication of them, “made it particularly dangerous for them.”

The complete Microsoft Entra ID would have given “god-tier” read and write access to all SharePoint sites and private employee OneDrive accounts, according to Nesbitt-Smith, including HR records. It also would have given access to sensitive libraries which safeguard evidence under legal hold for statutory planning inquiries and appeals, according to the security researcher who found it. “The option for ransomwaring them, for encrypting all the data, or just stealing all the data, was abundantly there,” Nesbitt-Smith says.

A spokesperson for the Planning Inspectorate told WIRED its cyber monitoring tools immediately detected Nesbitt-Smith’s activity in August and that it had already been handling this as a cyber incident when ControlPlane made contact. The agency identified and fixed this vulnerability within 20 minutes of the report and verified that no data breach occurred. “We have reviewed and strengthened our systems and processes to prevent this type of issue recurring and we are grateful for the researcher’s work and for alerting us to it,” they told WIRED.

The Planning Inspectorate issue “isn’t about open source but internal housekeeping when using public tools,” Amanda Brock, chief executive officer of nonprofit industry group OpenUK. “That data was exposed because of a failure not to follow good process,” she adds. “That’s not an open source security issue.”

In around two-thirds of the 349 public sector codebases across 33 organizations Nesbitt-Smith scanned, he said he found vulnerabilities. Several of these were found in the Department of Education’s code, including in a procurement service used by schools, in a teacher application service containing personal details, qualifications, employment history and identity documents, and England’s main register of government-funded training providers and apprenticeships. He also found a vulnerability in a Scottish Government open data portal which would have allowed any visitor to read administrative account information and to change site configuration. The organizations have since dealt with the issues.

Recently, there have been arguments for public sector departments to stop publishing source code in the open, now that AI has accelerated vulnerability discovery. The NHS reportedly ordered technology teams to transition away from open source code in May amid security concerns about the impact of AI models.

Doing this without immediately fixing the underlying issues would be the “worst case scenario,” according to Nesbitt-Smith, as it prevents researchers like him from finding them, and it’s likely that an adversary has already mirrored these repositories and so will maintain access to them. “Unless you’re going to go and fix all of the problems, if anything, you’re probably drawing more attention to it by closing it,” says Nesbitt-Smith, “because you’re like, ‘Here be dragons over this space. Don’t look here though, please.’”

Vulnerabilities & Patching.title: Google Issues Chrome Security Update for Eighth Actively Exploited Zero-Day of 2026
Vulnerabilities & Patching.context: Google on Monday released updates to patch nine security vulnerabilities, including one that has come under active exploitation in the wild. The high-severity vulnerability, assigned the CVE identifier CVE-2026-125350 (CVSS score: N/A), has been described as a use-after-free bug in the XML component
Vulnerabilities & Patching.full_text:
Google on Monday released updates to patch nine security vulnerabilities, including one that has come under active exploitation in the wild.

The high-severity vulnerability, assigned the CVE identifier CVE-2026-125350 (CVSS score: 8.8), has been described as a use-after-free bug in the XML component.

"Use-after-free in XML in Google Chrome prior to 157.0.8103.50 allowed a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code inside the sandbox via a crafted HTML page," reads the description of the flaw on CVE.org.

Use-after-free bugs typically occur when a program attempts to access a memory location after it has already been freed. Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities could allow an attacker to achieve data corruption, program crashes, or arbitrary code execution.

An anonymous security researcher has been credited with discovering and reporting the flaw on November 6, 2026.

Google acknowledged it is "aware that an exploit for CVE-2026-125350 exists in the wild," but has not revealed any additional specific information related to how it's being abused in real-world attacks or who is behind them.

"Access to bug details and links may be kept restricted until a majority of users are updated with a fix," the tech giant added. "We will also retain restrictions if the bug exists in a third-party library that other projects similarly depend on, but haven't yet fixed."

With the latest development, Google has addressed a total of eight actively exploited Chrome zero-days since the start of the year. This includes CVE-2026-2441, CVE-2026-3909, CVE-2026-3910, CVE-2026-5281, CVE-2026-11645, CVE-2026-85046, and CVE-2026-87491.

For optimal protection, users are advised to update their Chrome browser to versions 157.0.8103.50/.51 for Windows and Apple macOS, and 157.0.8103.50 for Linux. To ensure the latest updates are installed, users can navigate to More > Help > About Google Chrome and select Relaunch.

Users of other Chromium-based browsers, such as Microsoft Edge, Brave, Opera, and Vivaldi, are also advised to apply the fixes as and when they become available.

Update

The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added the Chrome vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, requiring federal agencies to apply the patch by November 24, 2026.

Vulnerabilities & Patching.title: N-able Takes N-central Cloud Offline After Researcher Discloses 33 Zero-Days with PoC Exploits
Vulnerabilities & Patching.context: N-able said it has taken N-central Hosted Environments offline and is urging on-premises customers to shut down their servers until further notice following the public disclosure of over 30 vulnerabilities collectively tracked as Able2Shell. "As a precautionary measure, we are temporarily taking our
Vulnerabilities & Patching.full_text:
N-able said it has taken N-central Hosted Environments offline and is urging on-premises customers to shut down their servers until further notice following the public disclosure of over 30 vulnerabilities collectively tracked as Able2Shell.

"As a precautionary measure, we are temporarily taking our Hosted N-central environment offline while we take the necessary actions to secure the environment and implement appropriate remediation," N-able said.

"During this time, customers will be unable to access their Hosted N-central classic environment, and associated services may be unavailable. However, the Ecoverse services under N-able Login remain available and online, including Asset View, Patching, Vulnerability Management, scripting, policies and tagging."

The company also said it has not observed any signs of active exploitation of these vulnerabilities, adding it's currently working on a hot fix to address them.

The following services are impacted -

N-central (hosted version) (Americas)

N-central (hosted version) (APAC)

N-central (hosted version) (Europe)

N-central On-premise (Americas)

N-central On-premise (APAC)

N-central On-premise (Europe)

The development comes as independent security researcher Sean Bales disclosed multiple security flaws along with proof-of-concept (PoC) exploits. The researcher said the issues were tested against N-able N-central Appliance 2026.4.0.31.

The identified zero-day vulnerabilities include credential disclosure, arbitrary file writes, directory traversal, cross-site scripting (XSS), XML external entity (XXE) injection, and remote code execution (RCE) flaws -

Multiple N-central zero-days enable anonymous credential theft, administrator creation, and nable/root RCE.

Chains include XXE/NCI trust abuse, support-token theft, unsigned NSP execution, XSS-to-OGNL, and authenticated reverse shells.

Arbitrary file writes, traversal, credential disclosure, MDM impersonation, audit tampering, and privileged-helper injection.

A native GenericTCP stack overflow also achieves root command execution

Successful exploitation of these flaws can allow rogue administrative access to the N-central management interface and facilitate command execution as root.

Update

watchTowr, in a post shared on X, said it "observed exploitation attempts against N-able N-central honeypots overnight following the 'Able2Shell' zero-days being dropped."

The preemptive exposure management firm is urging users to audit for signs of compromise, restrict access, and follow vendor guidance on mitigation steps.

In an X post, Defused Cyber said it has detected probing of N-able N-central for the Able2Shell zero-days. "We have seen opening of anonymous agent sessions, pulling appliance config and hitting the remote control endpoint without auth," it added. "These pathways are part of the 0-day exploit surface."

N-able has also confirmed that it's seeing "scanning activity associated with the published proof-of-concept code" but emphasized there is no evidence of successful exploitation in any customer environment.

The company has released N-central 2026.4 HF2 to address the following vulnerabilities. A follow-up hotfix is expected to be released to "provide further security updates" as part of its response to the Able2Shell disclosure.

CVE-2026-125883 - Multiple XXE Vulnerabilities

CVE-2026-125878 - Multiple OGNL Injection vulnerabilities

CVE-2026-125879 - Local privilege escalation to root via nable-writable syslog-ng config

CVE-2026-125880 - Stored XSS via MMS3 patch metadata (admin context)

CVE-2026-125881 - Schema-hint SSRF via service import schema validation

CVE-2026-125882 - RCE via file repository upload path traversal (Credit Nate Fair, Sprocket Security)

CVE-2026-91000 - Insecure IPC Channels lead to local privilege escalation

All Hosted N-central servers (NCODs) across all global regions have been upgraded. N-able is also urging customers to keep N-central servers offline until the updates have been successfully applied.

According to data from Censys, there are 1,728 internet-exposed N-central instances. Threat intelligence firm Previdian said it has recorded 68 exploitation attempts against one of its honeypots from a single IP address within about 18 hours of the publication.

Huntress is urging users to review login and authentication activity from November 8, 2026, onward for unexpected or unauthorized access, examine audit logs for secondary indicators of compromise, and apply N-able's hotfix and restore service only when N-able says it is safe.

Vulnerabilities & Patching.title: CISA Warns of Active Exploitation of OpenSSH, GPUStack, FreeSWITCH, and IBM Flaws
Vulnerabilities & Patching.context: According to GreyNoise, the first exploitation attempt against its honeypot network was observed on November 7, 2026, at 12:46 a
Vulnerabilities & Patching.full_text:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Monday added four security flaws impacting GPUStack, SignalWire FreeSwitch, OpenBSD OpenSSH, and IBM Aspera Faspex to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation.

The vulnerabilities are listed below -

CVE-2026-123218 (CVSS score: 9.8) - An incorrect authorization vulnerability in IBM Aspera Faspex that could allow an authenticated user to craft a specific message to bypass authorization, causing privilege escalations. (Fixed in November 2026)

CVE-2026-116779 (CVSS score: 9.8) - A code injection vulnerability in SignalWire FreeSwitch that could result in configuration and credential disclosure, arbitrary call control, and command execution. (Fixed in October 2026)

CVE-2026-123158 aka SSHole (CVSS score: 8.1) - An unexpected status code or return value vulnerability in OpenBSD OpenSSH on Linux that could allow for authentication bypass. (Fixed in November 2026)

CVE-2026-102895 (CVSS score: 9.8) - An improper authentication vulnerability in GPUStack that could allow improper authentication vulnerability which could allow unauthenticated administrative access, including user and model changes, persistent administrator API-key creation, disclosure of worker and cloud-provider secrets, and code execution through POST /v2/inference-backends/from-yaml. (Fixed in July 2026)

The addition of CVE-2026-123158 to the KEV catalog follows reports of exploitation attempts targeting the flaw since November 6, 2026. A total of 22 exploitation attempts have been recorded from 14 unique IP addresses so far, according to Previdian.

In a post shared on X on November 7, 2026, Defused Cyber said it "observed a small amount of actors targeting SSHole" but stressed the exploitation activity is not widespread yet.

According to GreyNoise, the first exploitation attempt against its honeypot network was observed on November 7, 2026, at 12:46 a.m. UTC. Confirmed post-exploitation activity has been detected from six source IP addresses, representing 18 distinct attack chains to date.

These involve reconnaissance, queries to cloud metadata services, attempts to read password hashes and root SSH keys, and efforts to modify the SSH authorized_keys file to gain persistent access.

In at least one case, an unknown threat actor dubbed GT10 has been observed deploying TAC Agent, a Python-based command-and-control (C2) agent capable of shell command execution, system reconnaissance, directory enumeration, file transfer, and updating itself.

Threat intelligence firm watchTowr said it has also observed the OpenSSH flaw being weaponized in the wild for botnet and cryptocurrency miner activity.

In an advisory for CVE-2026-102895 published on July 31, 2026, the maintainers of the GPUStack Python package credited Nikko Enggaliano, Wei Yunzhou, Rui Yang, and Haoyu Wang for independently reporting the flaw, adding that "active in-the-wild exploitation" was reported by Ulex Innovative Systems' Javier Sixto.

There are currently no public reports on how the other vulnerabilities are being exploited, who is behind them, and the scale of such efforts. Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies are recommended to apply the fixes by November 12, 2026.

Vulnerabilities & Patching.title: November 2026 Patch Tuesday: 1,252 CVEs Include One Zero-Day and 68 Critical Vulnerabilities
Vulnerabilities & Patching.context: November 2026 Attack Surface Analysis Preview-pane-triggered exploitation remains a dominant attack surface pattern for the third consecutive month, with eight Critical RCE...
Vulnerabilities & Patching.full_text:
November 2026 Attack Surface Analysis

Preview-pane-triggered exploitation remains a dominant attack surface pattern for the third consecutive month, with eight Critical RCE vulnerabilities across Microsoft Office applications including Outlook and Word. CVE-2026-110043 and CVE-2026-110068 in Outlook exemplify the risk: Merely selecting a malicious message in the Reading Pane or previewing an attachment in File Explorer triggers code execution without any click or macro prompt. This attack pattern continues to be attractive to phishing operators and initial access brokers because it converts document or message delivery into reliable code execution, bypassing the user-action barrier that many enterprises treat as a training backstop.

Identity platform components face elevated risk this month with Critical flaws in both Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) and Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS). CVE-2026-119958 enables RCE against LDAP, while CVE-2026-118146 and CVE-2026-118148 target AD DS with RCE and elevation-of-privilege attack paths, respectively. These protocols underpin domain authentication and authorization for every joined workstation and server; successful exploitation of either can cascade to domain-wide compromise. Similar identity fabric vulnerabilities have historically been targeted by advanced adversaries seeking persistent access to enterprise environments.

Windows Hyper-V sees an unusually high concentration of privilege escalation vulnerabilities this month, with eight CVEs spanning multiple flaw classes. CVE-2026-113753, CVE-2026-113856, and CVE-2026-113860 all enable elevation of privilege within the hypervisor boundary. Hyper-V underpins Azure compute infrastructure and endpoint features such as Windows Sandbox, Credential Guard, and other Virtualization-Based Security capabilities, so the exposure extends beyond dedicated virtualization hosts to ordinary Windows endpoints with these features enabled.

Legacy network services including Server Message Block (SMB) and Print Spooler continue to draw Critical-severity RCE findings, reinforcing the persistent risk these widely deployed components carry. The unauthenticated network-reachable RCE cluster spans 14 CVEs this month, with Windows Message Queuing (MSMQ) vulnerabilities such as CVE-2026-109459 and CVE-2026-116710 representing exposure on any system with MSMQ enabled. These services listen on the network by design and often lack authentication requirements for initial protocol negotiation, making any exposed instance an immediate target for opportunistic scanning. This class of legacy network service has historically been targeted in wormable exploitation scenarios.

Exploited Zero-Day Spoofing Vulnerability in Microsoft Outlook

CVE-2026-124194 is a Moderate spoofing vulnerability in Microsoft Outlook with a CVSS score of 6.5, and Microsoft confirms it is being exploited in the wild. The flaw stems from the product UI failing to warn users of unsafe actions: A specially crafted message file can cause Outlook to connect to an attacker-controlled network location without displaying the usual external-content warning, disclosing the victim's NTLMv2 hash.

Outlook is the default mail client across most enterprise Windows deployments, making any flaw that bypasses user safety prompts a direct initial access vector at scale. Exploitation requires the victim to open a malicious file delivered via email or another channel. The Preview Pane is not an attack vector for this particular CVE. Once the victim opens the file, Outlook silently initiates an outbound connection, and the captured NTLMv2 hash can be relayed or cracked offline to impersonate the user against other services that accept NTLM authentication.

The Moderate severity rating reflects the user interaction requirement, but the real-world exposure is broader than the score suggests. Credential disclosure flaws that require only a file open, bypass visible warnings, and yield reusable authentication material are a well-established technique in targeted intrusion campaigns. Similar spoofing primitives in Outlook have historically drawn attention from both commodity phishing operators and advanced adversaries seeking footholds in enterprise environments.

Critical RCE Vulnerabilities in Windows Services

CVE-2026-112967 and CVE-2026-116928 are Critical RCE vulnerabilities in Windows services, each carrying a CVSS score of 9.8. Both allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code over the network, though they affect distinct components with different deployment realities.

CVE-2026-112967 is a heap-based buffer overflow in the Windows Xbox Live Networking Service. An in-network attacker can call arbitrary endpoints on the service to trigger the flaw. Enterprise exposure depends on whether the service is present and running. Consumer-oriented Windows SKUs and gaming-enabled configurations are the primary population, making this lower priority for most corporate fleets.

CVE-2026-116928 is an out-of-bounds write in the Windows Search component. The attack path is notable: An unauthenticated attacker can send an email with a specially crafted attachment to an Exchange Server, and the search indexer processes the attachment automatically for indexing. The recipient does not need to open the email or attachment. Successful exploitation grants code execution with the permissions of the indexing service. Windows Search is broadly deployed and tightly integrated with Exchange for mailbox indexing, which places this flaw on an email delivery attack surface that reaches internet-facing mail infrastructure. The Windows Search path is the more significant exposure for enterprise environments. Email-delivered payloads that trigger without user interaction have historically been attractive to targeted intrusion operators because they bypass the phishing-click dependency that slows most initial access campaigns.

Critical RCE Vulnerability in Windows Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP)

CVE-2026-119958 is a Critical RCE vulnerability in Windows LDAP with a CVSS score of 9.8. The flaw is an out-of-bounds write that allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code by sending specially crafted LDAP calls to a listening server. No authentication or user interaction is required.

LDAP is the directory access protocol that underpins Active Directory. Every domain controller exposes LDAP on TCP/389 (and TCP/636 for LDAPS) by design, and the service cannot be disabled without breaking domain operations. Member servers, workstations, and applications query LDAP continuously for authentication, group policy retrieval, and object lookups, making it one of the most heavily trafficked protocols inside any AD environment.

The scope-of-impact concern is substantial. Code execution within the LDAP service on a domain controller places the attacker inside the trust boundary that every other domain resource relies on. From that position, credential extraction, replication abuse, and lateral movement to additional DCs become straightforward follow-on actions. Because LDAP is network-reachable from any domain-joined host by default, any internal foothold that can route to a DC can attempt exploitation.

Unauthenticated RCE flaws in core AD infrastructure have historically drawn rapid attention from ransomware operators and targeted intrusion actors because they collapse the gap between initial access and domain-wide compromise.

Preview Pane-Triggered RCE Vulnerabilities Across Microsoft Office

Eight Critical RCE vulnerabilities this month share a common attack vector: the Preview Pane in Outlook and Word. All carry CVSS scores of 7.5 to 8.8, with seven of the eight scoring 8.8. The underlying flaw classes are use-after-free (four CVEs), heap-based buffer overflow (two CVEs), release of invalid pointer (one CVE), and use of uninitialized resource (one CVE). Despite the variation in memory-corruption primitives, the exploitation pattern is uniform: An attacker delivers a malicious document or email, and merely selecting it for preview triggers code execution with the user's privileges.

The Outlook vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-110043, CVE-2026-110068, CVE-2026-111309) are the highest-exposure items in this group. Email is the delivery mechanism, and the Preview Pane is enabled by default in most enterprise Outlook deployments. An external attacker who can send mail to a target organization can reach the vulnerable code path without any authentication or prior foothold. The Word vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-110067, CVE-2026-111285, CVE-2026-124185) require document delivery, which typically means a phishing attachment or a link to a malicious file, but still fire on preview rather than open.

The remaining two CVEs (CVE-2026-111289, CVE-2026-120003) affect the broader Office suite and follow the same preview-triggered pattern. CVE-2026-124185 has a lower score (7.5) due to high attack complexity, but the others require no special conditions beyond user receipt of the malicious content.

Preview Pane vulnerabilities have historically been attractive to phishing operators and initial-access brokers because delivery converts directly to execution, with no need to persuade a user to open an attachment.

Critical Vulnerabilities in Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS)

CVE-2026-118146 and CVE-2026-118148 are Critical vulnerabilities in Active Directory Domain Services that both stem from incorrect authorization flaws. The two CVEs share a flaw class but differ in outcome and attack complexity.

CVE-2026-118146 carries a CVSS score of 8.8 and enables RCE. An authenticated attacker with low-level access to an affected server can send a specially crafted request and execute code without any user interaction. The authorization flaw means the server fails to properly validate that the authenticated principal should be permitted to perform the requested operation, turning a low-privilege foothold into code execution on a domain controller.

CVE-2026-118148 has a CVSS score of 7.5 and results in elevation of privilege to SYSTEM. This vulnerability has high attack complexity because successful exploitation requires the attacker to win a race condition. An authenticated attacker who can trigger the race gains SYSTEM privileges on the domain controller.

Active Directory Domain Services provides directory and authentication services for Windows enterprise domains. Domain controllers running AD DS issue Kerberos tickets, store the directory database, and process authentication and authorization decisions for every domain-joined resource. Compromise of a domain controller typically means compromise of the entire domain, since the attacker gains access to credential material and can issue arbitrary authentication assertions.

The attack surface for both vulnerabilities is any domain controller reachable from an authenticated low-privileged foothold. In most enterprise deployments, that includes every writable DC in the forest. Incorrect authorization flaws in identity platform components have historically been attractive to targeted intrusion operators because they convert commodity initial access into domain-wide compromise without requiring credential theft or additional tooling.

Critical RCE Vulnerability in Microsoft Exchange Server

CVE-2026-118207 is a Critical RCE vulnerability in Microsoft Exchange Server with a CVSS score of 8.8. The flaw stems from use of an incorrectly resolved name or reference, allowing an authenticated attacker with low-level access to send a specially crafted request and execute code on the server. No user interaction is required.

Microsoft Exchange Server provides enterprise email, calendar, and collaboration services, and is commonly deployed with internet-facing client access services for mobile and web users. The authentication requirement lowers the bar only modestly in most environments: Any compromised mailbox credential, service account, or partner federation relationship satisfies it. Once that requirement is met, the attacker reaches code execution on a server that typically holds sensitive mail content, internal address lists, and often enjoys elevated trust relationships with Active Directory.

Organizations running on-premises Exchange frequently expose Outlook Web Access, Exchange ActiveSync, and Autodiscover endpoints to the internet. Servers in this posture are reachable from any network position once the attacker obtains valid credentials, and successful exploitation yields a foothold inside the perimeter on infrastructure that processes sensitive communications.

Exchange Server vulnerabilities have historically drawn sustained attention from nation-state threat actors and ransomware operators because the combination of internet exposure, high-value data, and domain trust relationships makes compromised Exchange servers effective pivot points for broader intrusions.

Critical Elevation of Privilege Vulnerabilities in Windows Hyper-V

Microsoft addresses eight Critical elevation of privilege vulnerabilities in Windows Hyper-V this month, spanning five distinct flaw classes: use-after-free (four CVEs), heap-based buffer overflow (one CVE), TOCTOU race condition (one CVE), untrusted pointer dereference (one CVE), and use of uninitialized resource (one CVE). CVSS scores range from 6.4 to 8.2, with CVE-2026-113753 at the top of the range.

The exploitation outcomes fall into two categories. CVE-2026-113753 allows an attacker to gain Virtual Trust Level 1 (VTL1) privileges, which means escaping from the normal kernel (VTL0) into the secure kernel layer that underpins Virtualization-Based Security features such as Credential Guard. Five of the remaining seven CVEs enable guest-to-host escape: An attacker operating inside a guest virtual machine can execute code on the host in the security context of the virtual machine worker process.

Hyper-V is the hypervisor layer that runs Azure compute infrastructure and powers client-side Windows features including Windows Sandbox, Windows Subsystem for Linux 2, and Virtualization-Based Security. The exposure therefore reaches both datacenter server populations and ordinary endpoints where these features are enabled.

Most of the cluster carries a high attack complexity because exploitation requires winning a race condition, which raises the practical difficulty but does not eliminate the risk. Hypervisor escapes of this class have historically attracted attention from advanced adversaries because a successful exploit compromises the isolation boundary that separates tenants in shared infrastructure and protects credential material on endpoints.

Critical Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability in Windows Remote Desktop Services

CVE-2026-119957 is a Critical elevation of privilege vulnerability in Windows Remote Desktop Services with a CVSS score of 7.8. The flaw is a double-free that requires the attacker to win a race condition. Although exploitation is local, successful exploitation allows an attacker operating inside a guest virtual machine to escape to the host and gain the privileges of the affected virtualization service.

Remote Desktop Services underpins RDP-based remote administration across Windows Server deployments and is a core component in Virtual Desktop Infrastructure (VDI) environments. The guest-to-host escape path described in Microsoft's FAQ elevates this from a local privilege escalation to a potential hypervisor boundary violation, which matters in any multi-tenant or shared-host scenario.

The attack complexity is high due to the race condition. Post-compromise scenarios where an attacker already controls a guest VM provide the dwell time needed to attempt exploitation repeatedly. RDS-based session hosts and VDI pools present the most exposure to this guest-to-host escalation path.

Critical RCE Vulnerability in Windows SMB Server

CVE-2026-113825 is a Critical RCE vulnerability in the Windows SMB Server Network Transport Driver (srvnet.sys) with a CVSS score of 7.5. The flaw is a race condition that an authenticated attacker can trigger over the network to execute code. Microsoft notes that successful exploitation requires the attacker to win the race, which accounts for the high attack-complexity rating.

SMB is the native file-sharing protocol for Windows and is enabled by default on both client and server editions. The srvnet.sys driver handles the network transport layer for SMB traffic, sitting beneath the higher-level SMB2 and SMB3 protocol handlers. SMB listens on TCP/445 and is fundamental to domain operations such as SYSVOL replication, Group Policy delivery, and administrative shares.

The authentication requirement limits drive-by exploitation from the internet, but any attacker who has already obtained low-privileged domain credentials, or who operates from a compromised workstation, can attempt the race. Timing-based flaws in kernel-mode network drivers can be unreliable on a single attempt, yet become practical when an attacker can retry at scale across many hosts. Ransomware operators and targeted intrusion operators have historically exploited race-condition RCE flaws in legacy network services for lateral movement and wormable propagation.

Critical RCE Vulnerability in Windows Print Spooler

CVE-2026-113752 is a Critical RCE vulnerability in Windows Print Spooler with a CVSS score of 7.5. The flaw is a use-after-free that an unauthenticated attacker can trigger over an adjacent network. Successful exploitation requires winning a race condition, which raises the practical difficulty but does not eliminate the risk in contested LAN environments.

Windows Print Spooler manages print job queuing and driver loading on Windows endpoints and servers. It runs with SYSTEM privileges by default and is enabled on virtually every Windows installation, including workstations that have no physical printer attached. The adjacent-network attack vector limits exposure to attackers who already have a foothold on the same network segment, but that constraint is often satisfied during post-compromise lateral movement.

Print Spooler vulnerabilities have historically drawn sustained attacker attention because the service combines broad default deployment, high privilege, and a complex legacy codebase that has repeatedly yielded exploitable flaws.

Vulnerabilities & Patching.title: ZDI-26-906: X.Org Server libX11 XkbGetMap Reply Heap-based Buffer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
Vulnerabilities & Patching.context: Vulnerability Details This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of X
Vulnerabilities & Patching.full_text:
Vulnerability Details

This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of X.Org Server. User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must connect to a malicious X11 server.

The specific flaw exists within the XkbReadKeyActions function. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of the length of user-supplied data prior to copying it to a fixed-length heap-based buffer. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the current process.

Additional Details

X.Org has issued an update to correct this vulnerability. More details can be found at: https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/xorg/lib/libx11/-/merge_requests/309

Disclosure Timeline

2026-09-02 - Vulnerability reported to vendor

2026-11-10 - Coordinated public release of advisory

Anthropic's super bug-finding Mythos model is going into Cisco and IBM products
Vulnerabilities & Patching.context: Cisco will make it available under users’ existing licenses, without additional cost
Vulnerabilities & Patching.full_text: Anthropic has started extending access to its bug-finding Mythos model by allowing Cisco and IBM to make it part of their security products. Cisco announced its integration today at an event in Melbourne, Australia, where it revealed that the red teaming tools in its AI Defense suite, which looks for weaknesses and inappropriate activity in AI models, agents, and applications they power, will be able to call Mythos to test customers’ setups. “At a very high level, AI Defense has the ability to look at models and break them,” said Jeff Schultz, Cisco’s senior vice president for portfolio strategy and marketing. He said the tool is now “super-charged by Mythos” and will identify more danger that AI Defense will then address. AI Defense already uses AI-powered red teaming to find flaws. Mythos will become another option. Cisco will make it available under users’ existing licenses, without additional cost. Natalie Mead, Anthropic’s head of applied AI for the Asia-Pacific, said the company has a long queue of buyers who want to use Mythos, and working with Cisco will make it easier to satisfy that demand. Anthropic initially made Mythos available under "Project Glasswing," a program that gave vetted organizations access to the model to test their codebases, but has since expanded access through other controlled programs, an arrangement that makes considerable sense because in the wrong hands Mythos could help attackers exploit software flaws. The Cisco deal exposes the functionality of Mythos to end-users, without letting them use the model itself. The Register asked Mead if Anthropic has similar deals with other third parties and she demurred. That may be because a few hours after Cisco told us about its use of Mythos, IBM announced that it will also integrate Anthropic’s model into a product – namely its Concert tool, which uses AI to scan applications for risks and weaknesses. IBM says it will use Mythos “to uncover weaknesses traditional scanners miss, determine which pose real risk and generate fixes for developer approval.” We have asked Anthropic if these integrations represent a decision to open Mythos to more users in more ways. We will update this story if we receive a substantial response. Also on Monday, Anthropic introduced version 5.2 of Mythos and Fable, which the company says generate outputs up to 30 percent faster than version 5.1 yet cost less: $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens. Users can choose to run both models in “fast mode,” which speeds up token generation by up to 2.5 times, and doubles prices to $16 per million input tokens and $80 per million output tokens. Anthropic says it “ran extensive prerelease safety testing on the model that underlies Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2. This included developing novel evaluations that give deeper insight into specific concerning behaviors like sandbox escapes.” After those tests, the company concluded “high-stakes risks from misalignment remain low, and the model performed as well as, or better than, our recent models on most alignment measures. “Fable 5.2’s cyber and biology safeguards are as robust as those of Fable 5.1 but produce fewer unnecessary blocks, and we have implemented our strongest-ever protections against distillation attacks.” The latter is a telling admission, given Anthropic believes Chinese AI labs use distillation to effectively clone its models without doing expensive training work. ®

Vulnerabilities & Patching.full_text:
On November 9, 2026, a security researcher released a series of proof-of-concept (PoC) scripts targeting various vulnerabilities in N-able's N-central platform. The collection of PoCs claims to exploit several critical weaknesses in the N-central platform. As a result, N-able has taken the precautionary step of taking their N-central Hosted Environments offline.

At this time there is third-party reporting suggesting that exploitation is occurring in the wild. N-Able’s advisory does not indicate that they have observed exploitation as of this writing; however they do note that they have observed scanning activity associated with the published PoC code. At this time, Sophos X-Ops has not observed exploitation. We recommend that operators of on-premises N-central servers follow N-able’s advice.

Recommended actions

Sophos X-Ops recommends that organizations review N-able’s advisory and monitor it for further instructions from N-able.

Sophos countermeasures

SophosLabs continues to monitor the threat landscape for activity related to this threat and will deliver detections and protections as available.

Vulnerabilities & Patching.context: During previous N-central vulnerability exploitations (such as the CVE-2026-86218 zero-day), threat actors were observed "spraying" downstream environments with unauthorized...
Vulnerabilities & Patching.full_text:
Acknowledgments: Special thanks to John Hammond, Ben Bernstein, and Andrew Brandt for their contributions to this investigation and writeup.

Huntress is tracking N-able's response to the public disclosure of critical vulnerabilities in its N-central platform, a remote monitoring and management (RMM) platform built for managed service providers and IT teams. On November 9, N-able took its hosted N-central environment offline while it worked to secure the environment and apply remediation.

That move came after an independent researcher published the details of 33 critical vulnerabilities to GitHub that can be chained to lead to four different exploits (dubbed "Able2Shell"). Three of those chained exploits lead to remote code execution and one leads to privilege escalation to root. The vulnerabilities impact servers running N-central Appliance 2026.4.0.31 (and likely earlier versions as well).

N-able said it has not seen active exploitation of the vulnerabilities as of November 9 at 15:15:00 UTC. The company is working on a hotfix that it said will be available soon; customers should keep their N-central servers offline until N-able confirms they can be brought back online safely.

Huntress has tracked and responded to other, separate flaws in N-able's N-central this year, including five critical CVEs:

August 2026: N-able released a hotfix for CVE-2026-18556, a critical vulnerability impacting all current versions of N-central across both hosted and on‑prem deployments, giving attackers unauthenticated, "god-mode" access to the RMM console. CVE-2026-18577 was disclosed soon after as an incomplete patch to the former CVE.

September 2026: N-able issued a hotfix to address a third vulnerability, CVE-2026-86218, an actively exploited pre-auth RCE zero day with a 10.0 CVSS score. The next day Huntress produced a proof of concept (PoC) exploit of a separate, net new vulnerability chain (CVE-2026-86206 and CVE-2026-86207) in N-central that allowed attackers to bypass access controls to create unauthorized administrative accounts.

What Should Potentially Impacted Organizations Do?

Potentially impacted organizations should do the following:

If you run N-central on premises, take the server offline now and keep it offline until N-able confirms it is safe to restore.

If you use N-able's hosted service, expect an outage. N-able has taken its cloud infrastructure offline; follow its status page for updates.

Review login and authentication activity from November 8 onward for unexpected or unauthorized access. If you find suspicious activity, involve your incident-response team and assess whether systems or client networks managed through N-central may also be affected. The document warns that exploitation could enable remote code execution or privilege escalation on the server.

Carefully examine your audit logs for secondary indicators of compromise. During previous N-central vulnerability exploitations (such as the CVE-2026-86218 zero-day), threat actors were observed "spraying" downstream environments with unauthorized scripts and tools. Specifically, you should monitor for anomalous remote access sessions, new scripts being deployed, or the unauthorized creation of new administrator accounts.

Apply N-able's hotfix and restore service only when N-able says it is safe. The document said a hotfix was in development, with no exact ETA, so check current vendor guidance rather than relying on this dated update.

N-able does not always iterate version numbers when it pushes down live hotfixes that don't require a reboot, so it remains to be seen whether the patched version will be numbered 2026.4.0.31 or something different.

Next Steps

Huntress is actively investigating this incident and we are communicating with our potentially vulnerable customers to share updates as they become available. Please check this blog for further updates as we learn more information.

You can also get further updates from N-able at: https://uptime.n-able.com/event/202561/
