Miliefsky, Publisher of Cyber Defense Magazine.

Eliminate threats quickly and precisely with proven MDR.

Learn More

What sets LevelBlue MDR apart

As the world's largest pure-play managed security service provider, LevelBlue brings together intelligence-led security, AI-powered managed services, and deep cyber expertise to stop threats faster. Our MDR offering draws on the combined strengths of Trustwave, Cybereason and Alert Logic, each a long-standing name in detection and response, now united under one roof.

That combination gives customers:

Round-the-clock detection and response from experienced security operations teams

Threat intelligence that turns visibility across thousands of organizations into faster, better-informed action

Incident response readiness, so organizations know exactly what to do when an alert becomes an incident

Flexibility to protect cloud, hybrid and on-premises environments, including regulated and high-risk industries

A track record of recognition

This is the third year in a row that LevelBlue has been named a Top InfoSec Innovator, and the latest in a long run of Cyber Defense Magazine honors for the teams that now make up LevelBlue.

In 2025, LevelBlue was named Market Leader for Managed Security Service Provider (MSSP), Most Innovative for Threat Exposure Management and Publisher's Choice for Unified Threat Management. In 2024, we won Best Solution for MDR Provider, plus Publisher's Choice honors in Security Consulting and Threat Intelligence, and in 2023, AT&T Cybersecurity (now LevelBlue) was named Most Innovative in Threat Intelligence. Trustwave, now part of LevelBlue, built its own MDR track record in Cyber Defense Magazine's sister program, the Global InfoSec Awards, announced each spring at RSAC. It was named Market Leader for Global Managed Threat Detection and Response in 2021, Best Solution for both Cloud MDR Provider and Global MDR Service Provider in 2022, and Editor's Choice for MDR Service Providers in 2023. Across the two programs, LevelBlue and Trustwave have now been recognized for MDR in five of the last six years.

Thank you to our teams and customers

This recognition belongs to our security operations teams, who work around the clock to detect and stop threats, and to the customers who trust us to protect what matters most.

We're grateful to Cyber Defense Magazine and its judges for this recognition. To learn how LevelBlue MDR can help your organization detect and respond to threats faster, explore our MDR services or talk to an expert.

Business & Industry News.full_text:
I am delighted to announce CrowdStrike’s intent to acquire Fiddler at Fal.Con EU 2026. Fiddler, a leader in AI observability, will help ensure enterprise AI agents act as intended with pre-deployment evaluation and continuous behavioral monitoring as part of the CrowdStrike Falcon® platform.

Every business deploying AI agents asks the same questions: What are our agents doing? Are they staying on task? Are they acting in a way that could put the business at risk?

AI agents don’t have to be compromised to be dangerous. Those that stay within their guardrails can make a bad decision or take harmful action using valid credentials and approved enterprise tools. Businesses must be able to trace agents’ activity and explain anomalies as these concerns become top of mind among auditors, regulators, board members, and risk managers.

Enterprise AI safety requires a comprehensive approach: Evaluate agents before deployment, understand their decisions and actions, and continuously monitor their behavior. AI observability provides a lens into agent behavior before and after they ship. AI explainability shows why agents made their decisions and where their actions may have gone awry.

Fiddler delivers both. It will become part of the CrowdStrike Falcon® platform as CrowdStrike Falcon® Observe, generally available in Q4 FY27. With this acquisition, CrowdStrike will extend our AI security capabilities beyond protecting AI systems into proving businesses can safely use AI agents every day.

Building AI Trust in the Agentic Enterprise

Unlike traditional software, AI agents can make autonomous decisions, invoke tools, and take actions across enterprise systems. If software can act autonomously, security needs a record of those actions: what each agent decided, how it acted, what it changed, and the tools it used. They must know whether the agent made the correct decisions to follow its intended task.

As an example: Consider an AI agent using approved tools and valid credentials to process a customer refund. The agent makes an incorrect decision and approves a refund that violates company policy. Traditional security controls may see legitimate activity, but AI explainability reveals why the agent made that decision and where its behavior went wrong.

Fiddler provides AI observability for the agentic era. It helps organizations identify misaligned agents before they are deployed and continues to monitor agent behavior post-deployment so businesses have full visibility into what they’re doing and why.

Before deployment, teams can compare prompts, models, and configurations to evaluate whether agents perform intended tasks safely and accurately before they reach production.

After deployment, teams can trace agents’ decisions and reasoning paths across the full agent hierarchy to detect issues like behavioral drift and unintended actions before they cause harm. Fiddler reconstructs the agent’s decision-making process so teams can trace each failure to the step that caused it.

Fiddler supports auditable AI governance across organizations’ existing agents and tools. Its granular view of agents’ decision-making covers first-party and third-party agents across the enterprise so teams have the data they need to support compliance and audits. Businesses also gain explainability across the frameworks they run, as Fiddler enables teams to instrument agents through OpenTelemetry and supports LangGraph, Amazon Bedrock, AWS Strands, and Google ADK.

As part of the Falcon platform, Fiddler will connect AI agent intent and behavior with Falcon security telemetry across endpoints, identity, cloud, and runtime environments. This will help security teams understand why an agent took an action and what happened across the enterprise as a result. By connecting agent decisions with enterprise security context, CrowdStrike will provide visibility that goes beyond standalone AI observability.

CrowdStrike Delivers the Enterprise AI Control Plane

This milestone extends CrowdStrike’s leadership in protecting the agentic enterprise. Our acquisition of Fiddler, together with CrowdStrike Falcon® Guardian innovations announced today, will bring comprehensive AI security and safety solutions to the Falcon platform.

CrowdStrike can already establish AI agents as trusted identities, connect those identities to the humans operating them, grant access to business systems based on real-time risk, and secure AI agents at runtime. Fiddler will extend the Falcon platform to the earliest stages of the agent lifecycle, before deployment, to monitor their behavior before and after production, and explain the decisions they make.

Falcon Guardian protects AI agents from attacks and misuse. Falcon Observe evaluates and explains whether agents behave as intended. Together, they secure AI operations in the agentic enterprise.

There are a number of risks that could cause actual results to differ materially, including the satisfaction of the acquisition’s closing conditions, our ability to integrate Fiddler, and other risks described in the filings we make with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission from time to time.

Business & Industry News.context: Ransomware attacks are now a leading cybersecurity threat, with many pointing to the rise of crypto as an enabler
Business & Industry News.full_text:
October 30, 2026 – Published on The Wall Street Journal

Corporate cybersecurity leaders are having a schadenfreude moment after Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, lost billions of dollars this week to hackers.

Cryptocurrencies, like bitcoin, Ethereum and hundreds of others, have become the financial engine for ransomware attacks. By offering cybercriminals both speed and anonymity for collecting ransom payments, digital currencies have helped make ransomware into a booming underworld industry—and a major headache for chief information security officers.

On Thursday, Binance suspended transactions after hackers broke into the exchange’s platform and took off with more than $6 billion, marking the biggest cyber heist in history. The company said it is currently investigating the attack, which appears to have accessed systems through a worker’s laptop.

Ransomware attacks are now a leading cybersecurity threat, with many pointing to the rise of crypto as an enabler. But crypto isn’t the only factor behind the rise of the ransomware market. Among other issues, increasingly sophisticated phishing campaigns, new and wide-scale security vulnerabilities exposed by artificial intelligence and mounting geopolitical tensions have all played a role, cybersecurity experts say.Jason Baker, threat intelligence practice lead at GuidePoint Security, a cybersecurity services and incident response firm that helps companies negotiate with ransomware hackers, said crypto is a convenient scapegoat for beleaguered security chiefs.“You don’t blame cars if they’re the getaway vehicle for a bank robbery,” Baker said. And just as banning cars wouldn’t prevent bank robberies, he said, shutting down crypto platforms won’t stop hackers. “Threat actors adapt, and while this is a tool they’re used to, I think they’d adapt further away from cryptocurrency if they had to,” Baker said.Read More HERE.

Business & Industry News.full_text:
For the fifth consecutive year, Bitdefender is included as a Representative Vendor in the 2026 Gartner® Market Guide for Managed Detection and Response.

The Market Guide offers a timely opportunity to look beyond the table stakes of 24x7 alert monitoring and understand how modern MDR should leverage AI, how providers should help contain attacks, and the importance of MDR in reducing risk exposure.

As AI-enabled attacks become faster and more frequent, exposure reduction is a critical addition to detection and response.

What Do We Feel Inclusion In the 2026 Gartner® Market Guide for Managed Detection and Response Means?

Gartner says that more than 600 providers offer MDR services. The 30 vendors listed in the Market Guide meet the Gartner combined criteria for inclusion. Representative vendors:

Are consistently visible to Gartner clients (based on inquiries in the prior 18 months and through Gartner Peer Insights reviews from the prior 12 months)

Are variable in size and distribution to reflect the buying population

Have a clear end-user and outcome-focused offering distinct from pure technology-driven offerings

What Are Top Questions to Ask an MDR Vendor?

We believe three practical questions can help uncover whether a service is built around meaningful results.

How does the MDR vendor combine AI with human expertise to investigate threats and guide response decisions?

What actions will the MDR provider take automatically to contain an attack?

How will the MDR team help to identify weaknesses and reduce future risk?

We’ll look at these questions in detail below. They clarify whether a provider can help contain threats, reduce exposure, and support informed response decisions or if they primarily collect and escalate alerts.

MDR marketing claims can be challenging to sort out. According to Gartner: “Buyers continue to face challenges with service naming and marketing language that has often overpromised and underdelivered, adding confusion rather than clarity.”

What Is AI’s Optimal Role in MDR?

We believe AI should help security teams move faster, while people and threat intelligence guide investigations and response. According to Gartner:

“MDR must be people-focused, human-led, AI-augmented and anchored in the evidence of the successes and outcomes it delivers.”

Gartner also explains the value of this approach:

“But those services that combine automation with dynamic detection engineering and threat intelligence teams will continue to outpace an ‘automation-only’ mindset, identifying actionable countermeasures that combat the latest and most innovative threat actors.”

We believe Bitdefender MDR combines an AI-enabled SOC with round-the-clock human expertise. AI accelerates analysis and investigation, while security experts validate findings and oversee response decisions.

What Should MDR Do to Contain a Threat?

We believe an MDR provider should be ready to take agreed-upon action quickly, with clear authority and a plan to limit an attack’s spread. Alignment with your goals in this area is a key consideration for choosing the right vendor.

Gartner notes: “Assess how the MDR provider’s containment approach and incident reporting integrate with your organization. Also decide what type of actions will be performed on your behalf to align with business and compliance requirements, legal policies, and government regulations."

In our opinion, Bitdefender MDR uses pre-approved response actions to help contain threats, limit their spread, and minimize business disruption.

How Can MDR Help Reduce the Risk of an Incident?

MDR can support proactive risk and exposure reduction through threat hunting and prioritized guidance for addressing security weaknesses.

Notes Gartner: “Established MDR buyers routinely ask providers to extend their requirements beyond TDIR (threat detection and incident response) to include the proactive identification and mitigation of threat exposures.”

Bitdefender MDR leverages hundreds of millions of total covered endpoints to compile a massive amount of threat intelligence, attacker research, and threat analysis to continuously support threat hunts and update and protect customers. Our team of security experts also provides exposure insights that can help teams tackle underlying issues that might otherwise contribute to recurring risk.

Where Can You Learn More About Choosing an MDR Service?

The 2026 Gartner® Market Guide for Managed Detection and Response can help security and IT leaders assess the market against their organization’s needs.

Get complimentary access to the report to inform your next MDR decision. Then explore Bitdefender MDR to learn how we believe its AI-enabled SOC and security experts can help reduce exposure, contain attacks, and extend your team’s capabilities.

October 28, 2026 – Published on Axios

The cybersecurity world braced for catastrophe after AI uncovered critical flaws in the web’s foundational code, but the anticipated wave of automated attacks has surprisingly struggled to get off the ground.Why it matters: Millions of hacking attempts have yielded few successful attacks, an apparent lucky break due to the degree of difficulty of building attacks on the bugs. The defense work at many companies to address the issue also appears to have helped.That said, the sheer volume of AI-discovered bugs means the next era of cybersecurity will be defined by resilience — how quickly a company can detect an intruder, contain the damage and recover.The shift to building resilience doesn’t require throwing out the security playbook, however. Instead, companies should double down on basic cyber principles, such as using multi-factor authentication, Justin Timothy, threat intelligence consultant at GuidePoint Security, told Axios.Read More HERE.

Business & Industry News.full_text:
JFrog announced completion of the first-ever Software Supply Chain Excellence Awards, recognizing the teams who have turned their software supply chain into a competitive advantage – unifying development, security and operations around a governed, automated ecosystem that delivers trusted software at scale.

The nine honorees span the Americas, Europe, and Asia-Pacific, across three categories: Unified Platform, Trusted AI Adoption, and Software Supply Chain Security.

“Agents now write, review and deploy code faster than ever, while malicious AI models, agent skills and extensions are turning up in the registries developers use daily. Increasing regulations require proof at every step – from code to runtime,” said Roie Shorer, Chief Growth Officer at JFrog. “The companies that pull ahead in the AI era will be those going beyond simply automating for speed and scale. They will be the ones who can see exactly what’s shipping and why, as they bring trust, control and adaptability to their development operations. This year’s winners didn’t just add tools; they established a single source of truth where developers, security, and compliance teams can operate using the same data and the same rules. We’re very proud of all of them and thrilled to be part of their journey.”

Software supply chains are being put under new strain as developer teams grapple with AI-era software challenges. In its 2026 Software Supply Chain Security report, JFrog identified over 900 malicious AI agent skills carrying high-impact payloads alongside 495 malicious AI models on Hugging Face and 56 malicious extensions on OpenVSX. Attackers are no longer just targeting code; they are targeting the autonomous tools that write, review, and deploy it.

This year’s JFrog Software Supply Chain Excellence Award winners are working to reduce their exposure to these emerging threats by building a system of record that governs and secures artifacts from end-to-end – mastering the AI surge with speed and trust.

THE CONVERGENCE AWARD

The Convergence Award recognizes teams that unify a fragmented software delivery workflow – bringing previously disconnected repositories, scanners and tools into a single governed system of record.

Here are the winners:

Ford (Americas): Ford Motor Company has more than 15,000 developers spread across 80-plus global plants, which previously ran on separate repository tools and scanners with no shared visibility between them. By consolidating operations into a unified ecosystem with the JFrog Platform, Ford reduced tool sprawl and turned multiple blind spots into a single pane of glass view for IT and security teams. As a result, the team now manages more than 43 million artifacts on the JFrog Platform with 99.99% uptime. The team credits the consolidation with recapturing an estimated $8 million a year in developer productivity.

SCHOTTEL Industries (EMEA): Schottel replaced fragmented artifact storage and open-source consumption with the JFrog Platform. Over six months it delivered more than 32,000 artifacts, curated over 2,300 open-source packages and automatically blocked more than 900 risky ones. Manual dependency approval processes that previously delayed developers by months were replaced by automated governance and security controls, enabling faster adoption of new technologies while helping maintain its compliance and security standards.

Rakuten Symphony (APAC): Rakuten Symphony runs 28 self-hosted JFrog Enterprise+ instances across India, Japan and Singapore, that are all connected by JFrog Federated Repositories into one collaborative environment. With JFrog Curation and JFrog Advanced Security moving controls to the point of ingestion, the company cut manual triage efforts by roughly 60% in a single month across more than 600 releases, reclaiming more than 500 engineer-hours and pre-triaging over half of its vulnerability workload automatically.

THE TRUSTED INTELLIGENCE AWARD

The Trusted Intelligence Award recognizes teams that bring enterprise-grade governance to AI and model lifecycles, helping trust extend far beyond just supporting application code.

Here are the winners:

NVIDIA (Americas): Models repositories are under enterprise identity control, with a shared curation and scanning policy,which means a downloaded model faces the same checks as a package before it reaches production.

NVIDIA brought its AI model distribution surface under a governed perimeter by applying curation, scanning, and policy enforcement directly to its model mirrors. Thousands of AI model seats are now managed inside a controlled, auditable boundary, transforming what was once an unmanaged distribution surface into a demonstration of DevGovOps operating at true enterprise scale. To get there, NVIDIA leveraged JFrog Curation and JFrog’s scanning and policy tools, piloting them on the infrastructure through which its AI models flow.

Husqvarna Group (EMEA): Husqvarna’s autonomous divisions, across forest, garden and construction equipment, had accumulated overlapping scanners with limited shared visibility into software supply chain risk. After consolidating around the JFrog Platform and introducing software package scanning and policy-based controls earlier in the software development lifecycle, builds were progressively onboarded, providing teams with greater visibility into open-source dependencies and a more consistent approach to software component governance. Husqvarna Group validated JFrog Curation and JFrog Advanced Security in a hands-on pilot ahead of full deployment, and says the centralized visibility helps streamline security and governance workflows while supporting software traceability and reporting needs associated with evolving regulatory requirements, including the EU Cyber Resilience Act and NIS2.

Singapore Airlines (APAC): Singapore Airlines moved from “trust by verification” to “trust by default.” JFrog Curation and JFrog Xray now help intercept malicious, risky or non-compliant assets before they reach a build, including AI models, MCP servers, agent skills and IDE extensions. More than 95% of AI and open-source dependencies are onboarded through curated channels prior to integration. As a result, late-stage release blocks from non-compliant dependencies are down 60-75% and the airline has full visibility of its compliance posture.

THE GUARDIAN AWARD

The Guardian Award recognizes software supply chain security operating at real enterprise scale – blocking threats before they reach production across large, highly distributed environments.

Here are the winners:

S&P Global (Americas): S&P Global’s five divisions ran on independent JFrog Artifactory clusters with no shared policy enforcement which could potentially increase risk. By putting JFrog Curation at each point of ingestion – backed by continuous rescanning – S&P addressed that gap without slowing down development teams. Critical vulnerabilities across 30 images fell by 90%, from 141 to 14. S&P reports that about 99% of malicious npm and PyPI packages are now blocked at the point of ingestion, with JFrog Curation deployed as a synchronous gate for every division and JFrog Xray continuously rescanning artifacts already in use to catch newly disclosed threats.

TSB Bank (EMEA): TSB built a continuous governance platform based on JFrog’s APIs, using GitHub Actions and Open Policy Agent, as well as a versioned Python library published to JFrog Artifactory. Automated weekly audits check configuration drift, access control, artifact integrity and artifact authenticity. In the first seven months of using the platform there were 75 governance issues, 74 of which were resolved, with 11 production repositories verified for integrity every week.

Iress (APAC): Iress put the SaaS implementation of JFrog Artifactory at the center of their 600 developer operations, and added JFrog Curation and JFrog Xray to help keep zero-day threats from entering the development environment. In just eight months, the curation initiative mitigated six critical security incidents, while eliminating 90% of reactive vulnerability triage – saving the team an estimated 13,705 engineering hours for the year.

THE SELECTION PROCESS

Award winners were selected by a cross-functional panel of JFrog leaders and industry voices who scored each submission on the breadth of its story and the strength of its metrics. The complete list of winners and full category criteria are available at jfrog.com/software-supply-chain-awards.

You don’t have to be an award winner to experience the advantages of the JFrog Platform. Schedule a demo today and perhaps your team will be joining us on the podium next year.

Learn which capabilities helped us achieve our 8th consecutive recognition in the Gartner® Magic Quadrant™

Delinea has been named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Privileged Access Management (PAM) for the eighth consecutive time.

This is our eighth time running in the Leaders Quadrant, and it comes at a moment when the identity landscape looks nothing like it did even two years ago. Enterprises are no longer just managing human and machine identities. They're managing a fast-growing population of AI agents that need access to systems, data and each other, often with no human in the loop at all. We believe this year's recognition reflects how seriously we've taken that shift.

What changed this year

Over the past twelve months, we added just-in-time runtime authorization for AI agents. In plain terms, the same granular, time-bound access controls we've long applied to human and machine identities now extend to autonomous agents operating inside enterprise environments. An agent gets exactly the access it needs, exactly when it needs it and that access goes away the moment the task is done. Decisions are made in real-time and governed by policy.

The centralized control, session monitoring and credential management features are particularly valuable, as they help enforce strong security policies while maintaining smooth operational workflows. Lead Engineer - IT Services

We think this is what will be required for authorization going forward. Access shouldn't be a standing grant that sits around waiting to be misused. It should be a decision made in the moment, based on context and revoked automatically once that moment passes. The Gartner evaluation noted our placement on the Ability to Execute axis, and we believe our shift toward dynamic, real-time authorization is a major reason why.

Why this matters to you

If you're evaluating PAM vendors right now, here's the practical takeaway: The market is being reshaped by AI agents faster than most security programs are ready for. Every agent your teams deploy is a new identity that needs governing, and static, standing access to critical infrastructure. This is exactly the kind of attack surface that gets exploited. We feel a Leader placement is just that. We see it as an independent signal from Gartner that a vendor's approach to this problem holds up in the market on both vision and execution.

Delinea Secret Server has consistently demonstrated its value as a comprehensive and scalable PAM solution. Director, IT Security and Risk Management - IT Services

For customers already on the Delinea Platform, we feel this validates the direction we've been building toward: authorization that happens at the moment of access and built on defendable policies, not before it and not as an afterthought. For prospects comparing options, it's a data point worth weighing alongside your own evaluation, not a substitute for it.

Where we believe Gartner evaluates us

Just-in-time (JIT) PAM has emerged as a core capability to counter potential rogue agentic AI. Delinea has delivered enhanced cloud-native JIT capabilities along with protocol-level ephemeral credential injection for servers, databases and Kubernetes. In practice, this means credentials are issued at the protocol level for the exact moment they're needed and never persist as standing access.

That eliminates a huge chunk of the attack surface that traditional privileged credentials create, because there's no credential sitting around to be stolen, harvested or forgotten about.

This is the same philosophy extended across three populations at once: humans (workforce), machines (workload) and now AI agents. One authorization model, applied consistently, rather than three separate systems bolted together.

Reliability isn’t an afterthought

None of this matters if the platform isn't there when you need it. We guarantee a 99.995% monthly availability SLA across our global regions, including the US, EU, Canada, Southeast Asia, the UK, Australia, and the UAE. When you're enforcing access controls at scale, and especially when those controls are making real-time decisions for AI agents, the platform making those decisions has to be dependable. We treat that as table stakes, not a bonus feature.

Customer experience as a differentiator

We've heard directly from customers that what sets Delinea apart isn't just the technology; it's how straightforward the platform is to deploy, how much support is available when questions come up, how clearly we help teams understand where they sit on the maturity curve and what to tackle next. Mapping against 70 real-world use cases isn't a marketing exercise; it's a practical tool that helps security teams figure out what "good" looks like in their specific environment, rather than guessing.

Delinea is a trusted partner of ours. We have received first-class product support and service through the years. Our organization values this vendor relationship. IT Security & Risk Management Associate - Banking

Looking ahead

Eight consecutive times as a Leader is a recognition we don't take lightly, and it's also not the finish line. The identity landscape keeps moving. AI agents are only going to multiply, attackers are already using AI to move faster and the organizations that get ahead of this will be the ones treating authorization as something dynamic and continuous rather than something you configure once and forget.

We plan to keep building in that direction by extending runtime authorization further, tightening the connection between identity context and access decisions and making sure that whatever population of identities shows up next in your environment, AI agent, human or machine, gets governed with the same rigor.

Get complimentary access to the full 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Privileged Access Management and learn more about Delinea's recognition as a Leader.

Business & Industry News.full_text:
TrendAI™ runs NVIDIA Nemotron open models entirely inside customer-controlled infrastructure, delivering AI-driven threat detection and policy-based response without security data ever leaving the sovereign boundary.

DALLAS, Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TrendAI™, the global AI security leader and enterprise business unit of Trend Micro Incorporated (TYO: 4704; TSE: 4704), today announced it is bringing NVIDIA Nemotron™ open models into TrendAI Vision One™ for Sovereign and Private Cloud (SPC), building on its collaboration with NVIDIA. The integration brings AI-assisted security operations into customer-controlled environments, extending capabilities such as guided investigation, security reasoning, and agentic SIEM to organizations with sovereignty, data residency and operational control.

TrendAI Vision One™ for Sovereign and Private Cloud (SPC) is available today, enabling organizations to deploy TrendAI Vision One™ in customer-controlled private cloud, sovereign cloud and on-premises environments. The Nemotron integration extends AI-assisted security operations into these environments while maintaining customer control over security data and deployment.

Why Open Models Matter for SovereigntyHighly regulated organizations need AI-driven security that fits their data-control requirements. Nemotron open models can support these requirements by bringing the model to the data rather than the data to the model. Customers decide where the model runs, which version is deployed, and who can access it, running AI-powered security operations on NVIDIA accelerated computing in their own data centers, sovereign clouds, and restricted-connectivity environments. TrendAI™ collaboration with NVIDIA on OpenShell provides an additional level of security for agents, ensuring organizations have control and visibility of agentic activities.

Who Controls the Intelligence Acting on Your Data?"Sovereignty extends beyond where data resides. Enterprises also need control over where the intelligence acting on that data operates, and how it is governed." says Rachel Jin, CEO, TrendAI™. "Organizations shouldn't have to give up the operational benefits of AI because their security data and operations need to remain within a customer-controlled environment. Our work is about bringing AI-powered security operations to the environments our customers choose to control."

"Open models give organizations the transparency and control to run on their own terms, which is critical for sovereign environments," said John Fanelli, Vice President, Enterprise Software at NVIDIA. "TrendAI's integration of NVIDIA Nemotron models enables enterprises to put their most sensitive data to work, without it ever leaving their control."

Customer Perspective: Sovereignty Without CompromiseTITECH, which delivers sovereign security operations to customers in Oman, is working with TrendAI™ as a design partner on the Nemotron integration ahead of general availability.

"TrendAI Vision One for Sovereign and Private Cloud has provided our local customers in Oman with a trusted foundation for keeping security operations under customer control while complying with country data residency regulations," says TITECH CEO, Mohammed Hassan. "Nemotron-powered capabilities will let us offer advanced threat analysis and AI-assisted security operations to our customers while maintaining data sovereignty and operational control."

The integration supports AI-assisted threat analysis, policy-based response, and guided security operations within customer-controlled environments. These capabilities help organizations improve security operations with AI while maintaining control over where security data and AI processing reside.

Customer Outcome: Security and control from the start"As enterprises apply AI to real-world deployment, security and control must be embedded into the infrastructure from day one," says Business Manager of Security at Bechtle AG, Mathias Schick. "Our customers want to harness the full potential of AI without compromising data sovereignty, security, or operational control. Integrating AI-powered security into sovereign and private-cloud environments is an important step toward enabling secure AI adoption at scale, particularly for organizations with stringent security and compliance requirements."

TrendAI Vision One™ for Sovereign and Private Cloud (SPC) with NVIDIA Nemotron integration supports:

Customer-controlled AI: NVIDIA Nemotron open models deployed and run on customer-controlled infrastructure, with no dependency on external inference services

AI-assisted threat analysis: Reasoning across security signals to identify complex threat patterns, attack chains, and AI-native attack paths

Policy-based threat response: Supporting protective actions through organization-defined policies and security-team controls

Guided security operations: Helping security teams investigate threats and prioritize response activities

Agentic SIEM capabilities: Correlating telemetry and assisting with security reasoning while maintaining team oversight

TrendAI Vision One™ for Sovereign and Private Cloud (SPC) is available today. Visit trendaisecurity.com/platform/sovereign-private-cloud or visit TrendAI™ at NVIDIA GTC Berlin's expo (October 21-22, 2026) to preview these planned capabilities.

About TrendAI™TrendAI™, the global AI security leader and enterprise business unit of Trend Micro, empowers organizations with full AI visibility, governance, and consolidated security that inspires confidence, drive innovation, and eliminate risk. Trusted by the largest enterprises and governments across 185 countries, TrendAI™ secures the entire organization, from identities to infrastructure to data. Global Fortune 500 companies rely on TrendAI™ to stop threats up to 115 days earlier, powered by world-leading threat and attack intelligence. Through deep ecosystem partnerships with market leaders like NVIDIA, Anthropic, AWS, Google, and Microsoft, TrendAI™ enables teams to securely move at the speed of AI. AI Fearlessly. Learn more at trendaisecurity.com.

Business & Industry News.context: It is common practice for tech companies to offer escalating compensation awards to their executives
Business & Industry News.full_text:
Today, we’re committing a portion of Anthropic’s shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a new wholly owned entity with a structure that increases the stake as the company grows. Subject to stockholder approval, 5% of Anthropic’s shares will be committed today, with an additional 2% added at the board’s discretion for every 50% increase in the company’s value above a set baseline.

As a public benefit corporation, most of our work in pursuit of our mission takes place inside the company: research relevant to AI safety and interpretability; applied biomedical research; discounts on Claude for nonprofits and scientific institutions. These activities have both a public benefit component and for-profit value, so we house them directly in the company.

The Anthropic Public Benefit Fund will have increased flexibility and scale, enabling us to pursue our mission in new ways: for example, we might explore large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations.

One example is labor market impacts. AI may generate enormous economic value, but it could also cause instability for many workers. Anthropic has already committed $200 million to studying and addressing this issue, but given the pace of AI progress, bolder approaches may be needed. The Fund will have the versatility to pursue them.

We’re establishing the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund as an LLC—rather than a 501(c)(3) or other format—to give adjustability between different forms of giving. None of the Anthropic equity held by the LLC will be used for lobbying or political giving, in the US or abroad.

Because of the way the Fund is structured, the more Anthropic grows, the larger the share of the company that can be dedicated expressly to the public good. It is common practice for tech companies to offer escalating compensation awards to their executives. We are instead directing that equity to the public benefit.

This builds on commitments our co-founders and employees have already made. When Anthropic was founded, our co-founders pledged to donate 80% of their equity holdings, and since founding we have also operated an equity donation match program that allows employees to pledge equity which Anthropic matches. Approximately half of our employees participate in this program. When combined with today’s announcement, roughly 20% of Anthropic shares will be dedicated to the public good, plus any additional percentage that could be added if the company reaches specific valuation milestones.

In the coming months, we will share more about the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund’s structure and governance, including the valuation milestones that may add to its stake. We will also report on our progress to date against our mission in an upcoming public benefit report.

Business & Industry News.title: Proofpoint CEO Sumit Dhawan On ‘Market-Changing’ $6.3B Varonis Deal, IPO Goal
Business & Industry News.context: 3 billion deal for publicly traded Varonis was announced—Dhawan said that the planned acquisition seeks to bring together complementary technologies for securing data and AI...
Business & Industry News.full_text:
The planned acquisition of publicly traded data security vendor Varonis will enable Proofpoint partners to deliver a ‘comprehensive data security solution to their customers,’ which is primed for combating AI and agentic risk, Dhawan tells CRN.

Amid the surging adoption of AI agents, Proofpoint’s “market-changing” deal to acquire Varonis is aimed squarely at helping partners and customers to protect the data those agents can access, Proofpoint CEO Sumit Dhawan told CRN.

In an interview Friday—a day after Proofpoint’s $6.3 billion deal for publicly traded Varonis was announced—Dhawan said that the planned acquisition seeks to bring together complementary technologies for securing data and AI agents, while giving partners an even more strategic role with their customers.

[Related: 5 Things To Know On Proofpoint’s $6.3B Acquisition Of Varonis]

The deal ultimately is positioned to enable Proofpoint partners to deliver customers a broader data security platform that is primed for combating AI and agentic risk, he said.

With the combined Proofpoint-Varonis platform that is envisioned, partners will be enabled to “take a comprehensive data security solution to their customers—becoming more strategic, providing more value-added services,” Dhawan said. “And No. 2, they now can work with a single [data security] provider with a larger business.”

The combination of Varonis with Proofpoint, which was itself publicly traded until its acquisition by private equity firm Thoma Bravo in 2021, is also poised to strengthen Proofpoint’s positioning for an initial public offering, Dhawan told CRN.

“We think it’s going to be even more attractive to public investors, and our goal would be to assess that after close,” he said.

The combined company would have more than 8,000 employees with annual recurring revenue (ARR) of more than $3 billion, according to figures disclosed by the companies.

Upon completion of the combination of the two vendors, “it’s a top-five cybersecurity company with healthy growth—and more importantly, [providing] the next frontier of protection, which is data,” Dhawan said.

What follows is more of CRN’s interview with Dhawan.

What does this deal mean for the industry and the channel?

It’s a game-changing moment—just bringing together Varonis and Proofpoint makes us the [premier] data security solution in the market, especially in the world of AI. So we’re very excited.

It sounds like the ultimate plan is for this to be a combined solution from the two companies, as opposed to being Varonis operating independently of Proofpoint?

[Varonis CEO] Yaki [Faitelson] and I started the conversations a while ago. And we always compare notes on the market and whatnot. [We are] largely complementary. And earlier this year, as this whole agentic era starts shaping up, we said, look, there is clearly a next frontier on cybersecurity emerging, which is data. AI is attacking data from outside, and AI is attacking data [from] inside. And data protection needs to be done holistically. That was the vision that brought us together—to say, not just that we can have one house that will be able to serve all the portfolio. But if you’re really providing data protection, it needs to be done with machine speed. And machine-speed level of protection, in the world of AI, means integrations of our signals and control points. And that’s what our vision is. We believe we can accomplish that very, very quickly, based on just how complementary our technology stack is.

What are you hearing from your customers and your partners about how urgent of a need there is for something like this?

The whole conviction of ours is rooted on the principle that this is a board- and CEO-level priority. [When] you think about it, AI and cybersecurity, those are the two priorities for the board and CEOs. And they go hand-in-hand. Without data security, you can’t enable and adopt AI. So to me, that sort of is the grounding fact for the conviction that we have, on why data becomes the next frontier for cybersecurity—and why Proofpoint and Varonis becomes the only player that no other [vendor] can do, [providing] a full and comprehensive solution for protecting data in today’s AI-accelerated risks.

Can you say whether the combined company will operate entirely under the Proofpoint brand, or whether Varonis will still exist as a brand in some form?

We’re going to talk through it—we’re going to think that through. Those things get sorted out as we go. [Both companies have a] strong product, strong following in the customer base. So we don’t have any desired intent to make one change or the other. But it’s something we’ll figure out between now and close [of the deal].

As far as what Varonis brings in product capabilities, what specifically are you most excited about? And what do you think partners are going to be really excited about from Varonis?

What Proofpoint has built is sensing how people and AI behave when they’re interacting with data and each other—that’s our focus area. Intent-based protection, as we’ve always talked about, when people, AI and data come together. What Varonis has built is making sure that [businesses understand] where the data is and how it is getting protected based on privileges and usage. So these are a complementary set of signals. We are getting the signals on the intent and behavior, and they’re getting the signals at the data layer. Combining the two together gives you the right protection of data in today’s AI and machine-speed era. That’s the complementary nature of the solution. I’ve gotten so many positive feedback in less than 24 hours, and it’s all been about this—[they’ve been] waiting for [a vendor] who brings data security together. And Proofpoint and Varonis, because of the complementary nature of the solution, [can] become that company.

It sounds like some of the capabilities that Varonis has in certain areas are bringing something a bit different to your platform?

We already have data security solutions. We’re the market leader for DLP [data loss prevention]. We’re the market leader for insider risk solution. Those are complementary to the data security and access governance solution that Varonis brings. You combine them together, and now you can protect data at rest, and you can protect data in motion, as used by humans and AI. So think of it as data security at two different layers, working together, through a combination of signals and protection.

Are you saying how many employees the combined company will have?

Varonis has more than 2,500 employees [and] publicly we have said we have closer to 5,500 employees. As a combined company, it’s an at-scale company. We have publicly said that our ARR exiting midyear was closer to $2.5 billion. They have publicly said a little shy of $800 million exiting June. So you’re talking about a company of scale. It’s a top-five cybersecurity company with healthy growth—and more importantly, [providing] the next frontier of protection, which is data.

Envisioning the bringing together and combining of these two companies, you would say this is going to be very differentiated?

If you look at other top-five cybersecurity companies, none of those platforms were designed and built to do data protection. They’re [from] different eras of cybersecurity—endpoint, network. We become, together, the company that protects data from external threats as well as insiders. Both are being accelerated because of AI.

On the partner front, what should partners of both companies know about what this means?

Partners are excited. It happened to be that yesterday we had a European partner council, and our head of Europe was running that partner council when the news broke. And many of them said, “Hey, look, Varonis is one of our top partners. Proofpoint is one of our top partners. Together, you become maybe the No. 1 or No. 2 partner of ours going forward.” From a partner’s perspective, No. 1, most importantly, they can take a comprehensive data security solution to their customers—becoming more strategic, providing more value-added services. And No. 2, they now can work with a single provider with a larger business—which is what partners want, anyway.

Previously you talked about potentially going public at some point—probably it’s not something you would be looking at doing prior to closing this, but is there any update there?

Like you said, our focus is going to be on [closing the acquisition]. And we hope to go through the regulatory process and close the transaction as early as possible. And then we think that the combined company is quite attractive to the public investors. It’s an at-scale company, driving protection of one of the key pillars, just like any other major cybersecurity platforms are doing. We think it’s going to be even more attractive to public investors. And our goal would be to assess that after close.

Agents are something that so many businesses are grappling with, and it sounds like this combination is very much going to be tuned toward helping companies with that?

Exactly. There isn’t a day that goes by whereby we don’t read the news about risks that AI agents pose. Risks that AI agents pose doesn’t mean you have to slow down the adoption. It just means that you need to adopt AI with the right degree of security. What are these risks going after? You read all these stories. Eventually, the issue is that these AI agents go to data [systems], and the data is captured in so many different places. So enterprises need comprehensive solution that can both work on protecting the behavior of AI and protecting the data, regardless of where it exists. And that’s what Proofpoint and Varonis offers. It provides a solution that enables enterprises to go pick any agents of their choice. They’re not locked in. Go pick and enable access to any data of their choice. And in that environment, their data is protected, and they can adopt AI with speed.

There are so many different vendors coming out and saying they’re going to have some solution to this. But it sounds like part of the idea here is if you’re already protecting the data—as you and Varonis are—then you’re really in the best position to help with the agent problem, if the agent is ultimately trying to access data?

That’s 100-percent right. There is no use solving a sliver of the problem. These are interconnected problems—because eventually, agents have to access data. By protecting data, you extend that protection to protecting AI agents. So that’s why our solution in protecting agentic security—through an extension of protecting data—becomes even more powerful and real for customers.

Overall, what is the message for your partners out of this, and what is the major opportunity for them?

Firstly, I want to thank the partners that have really built the business for us. We couldn’t do it without them. And this is game-changing. It’s a market-changing, game-changing [deal], really helping customers together with partners. We can be their strategic advisors, a platform for protecting the next frontier of cybersecurity, which is data, and all driven because of AI.

Policy, Legal & Compliance.context: Europol’s 2026 Internet Organised Crime Threat Assessment names the replacement of shut-down markets as a current trend, with criminals moving fast to new platforms
Policy, Legal & Compliance.full_text:
Europol and police in 14 countries arrested 354 dark web vendors and buyers in Operation TorNado, which ran from May 2025 to October 2026. Investigators went after people who had traded on five marketplaces that were already offline: Archetyp, Bohemia, Nemesis, Kingdom and Tor2Door.

Seized money (Source: Europol)

The people who used those markets were still exposed after the sites went dark. Police also went after vendors and buyers on forums, single-vendor shops and encrypted messaging services, and carried out hundreds of house searches.

The US made the most arrests

The United States made 132 of the arrests. The UK followed with 59, then Hungary with 45 and Germany with 41. Finland made one arrest and conducted 159 interrogations.

US authorities seized more than 4.8 metric tonnes of drugs, 152 firearms and over €150 million in cash and cryptocurrency. In Europe, police seized 950 kilograms of drugs, 57 firearms, more than one million prescription tablets and over €60 million in cash and crypto. The US drug haul is about five times the size of Europe’s.

Europol traced the money

Europol sent staff to Czechia and Slovenia during the operation. It also coordinated the national cases so investigators didn’t end up chasing the same suspects twice. Its blockchain analysts traced the illegal transactions.

New markets keep appearing

TorNado follows earlier Europol operations, including RapTor in 2025, SpecTor in 2023, Dark Huntor in 2021 and DisrupTor in 2020. Europol’s 2026 Internet Organised Crime Threat Assessment names the replacement of shut-down markets as a current trend, with criminals moving fast to new platforms. The same assessment says marketplaces are splitting into platforms that each focus on one kind of crime.

Policy, Legal & Compliance.title: Operation Endgame Takes Down Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC Servers, Seizes 6.4M Stolen Logins
Policy, Legal & Compliance.context: Criminals used the three malware tools to gain access to computers, steal passwords, and launch ransomware attacks
Policy, Legal & Compliance.full_text:
An international police operation took down servers behind Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC this week. Criminals used the three malware tools to gain access to computers, steal passwords, and launch ransomware attacks.

Police also seized about 6.4 million stolen logins belonging to more than 40,000 victims, according to Germany's Federal Criminal Police Office (BKA).

Gootloader is a loader: once on a computer, it could download other malware, especially ransomware. It spread through fake legal documents placed on hacked websites, often WordPress sites. Criminals used SEO poisoning to push those sites high in search results.

Gootloader has infected at least 25,000 computers worldwide since 2018, the U.S. Justice Department said. Its operators used those computers to infect more computers, then sold access to the new ones to ransomware criminals. In the U.S., Gootloader was used in ransomware attacks against at least 44 victims, resulting in about $28.8 million in losses.

German police gave a much higher count in their statement in German. Based on what investigators know so far, Gootloader has infected millions of computers worldwide since it first appeared in 2020.

Across the three tools, police seized 235 servers and 257 domains, according to an operation summary from Europol, which supported the action. The takedown is part of Operation Endgame, an international police campaign against malware criminals use to access victims' computers.

For Gootloader, police took down 14 servers and 218 domains and removed malware from 681 hacked websites.

With court approval, U.S. agencies and their international partners removed Gootloader from more than 100 servers, including hacked WordPress sites. They also seized U.S. domains used to deliver and control the malware, according to the Justice Department announcement.

CastleRAT, a remote access trojan (RAT) known since 2025, allows attackers to control an infected computer remotely. Police seized 120 of its servers and 39 domains.

StealC is an infostealer that exfiltrates passwords and other login credentials from infected computers, allowing criminals to sell or misuse them. Police took down its servers again this week, after a June operation against it.

After that June action, its operators changed their infrastructure and brought it back online to stay out of investigators' reach, German police said. Some of StealC's key infrastructure ran on Virtualine/Omegatech, a bulletproof hosting service that advertised its services to criminals.

Police shut that hosting service down in a late-October takedown.

No arrests were announced in this week's action. Dutch police also carried out further investigations targeting Gootloader's main suspect, according to their news release.

What Victims and Site Owners Can Do

Dutch police have loaded data stolen by CastleRAT into Check your hack, a police service where people can enter an email address. If the address is in the data, the police send an email within a few minutes with steps to remove the malware. If it is not, no email arrives.

More data will be added in the coming weeks. The service checks single addresses, not whole domains, but organizations can join No More Leaks, a police project that shares data with private partners. The stolen data is also being shared with services including Have I Been Pwned and the Shadowserver Foundation.

Emails that claim to come from the police and ask people to check the data are fake. The police never send emails with links.

Even after police seize the data, criminals may still have the stolen logins, the police say in their frequently asked questions. As long as the malware stays on a computer, criminals may also keep getting its passwords.

The Shadowserver Foundation is working with internet service providers and computer security incident response teams (CSIRTs) to find infected computers and notify their owners, the Justice Department said. In Germany, the Federal Office for Information Security (BSI) is helping notify victims, according to the BKA.

Denmark's National Special Crime Unit (NSK) helped clean the 681 websites. In a statement in Danish, the unit said it believes the attackers got into the sites with stolen passwords that came through criminal channels. They then installed a backdoor.

Officers removed the attackers' code and access, and left a message for the site owners with advice on securing their sites.

Police in Denmark and the Netherlands advise WordPress site owners to take these steps, several of which are set out in a Dutch advice sheet:

Change all administrator passwords to unique, at least 12-character passwords.

Turn on multi-factor authentication (MFA).

Remove accounts you do not recognize.

Remove any backdoor code from the site.

Update WordPress, its themes, and its plugins.

Allow access to the /wp-admin login page only from the IP addresses of your own devices.

Policy, Legal & Compliance.title: Law Enforcement Disrupts Gootloader, CastleRAT, and StealC Infrastructure
Policy, Legal & Compliance.context: Law enforcement agencies in the US, Europe, Australia, and Canada have seized infrastructure behind the notorious Gootloader, CastleRAT, and StealC malware
Policy, Legal & Compliance.full_text:
Law enforcement agencies in the US, Europe, Australia, and Canada have seized infrastructure behind the notorious Gootloader, CastleRAT, and StealC malware.

The investigators seized 235 servers and 257 domains associated with the malicious operations, severely crippling their distribution networks, Europol says.

Operating under the cybercrime-as-a-service model, Gootloader, CastleRAT, and StealC enabled ransomware attacks, data theft, and other cybercrime activities.

Distributed through compromised websites containing fake legal documents, Gootloader has been operating as a dropper for other malware families, including ransomware.

Active since at least 2018, Gootloader has infected over 25,000 computers and caused damages of approximately $28.8 million in the US, the US Department of Justice says.

According to the DoJ, the fresh disruption, part of Operation Endgame, led to the dropper’s removal from 100 servers. Europol reports that 14 servers and 218 domains associated with Gootloader were seized and 681 infected websites were cleaned up.

Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.

A remote access trojan (RAT) active since at least 2025, CastleRAT has provided threat actors with control over infected machines, which were then abused to deploy file-encrypting ransomware.

Law enforcement seized 120 servers and 39 domains used by CastleRAT’s operators, as well as victim data. HaveIBeenPwned says 180,000 email addresses and 893,000 unique passwords were retrieved.

Active since at least 2023, StealC functions as a stealer and a dropper, mainly focused on password, data, and identity theft. In a continuation of law enforcement action targeting the malware earlier this year, 102 StealC servers were disrupted.

According to Europol, the fresh law enforcement disruption led to the seizure of 6.4 million victim credentials, which have been shared with HaveIBeenPwned, DIVD, CheckjeHack, NoMoreLeaks, Sekoia, The Shadowserver Foundation, and NL-NCSC.

“The suspects were using these credentials, stolen from the victims after they infected them, to sell them and later be used for other cyber-attacks such as ransomware,” Europol notes.

Policy, Legal & Compliance.title: Brit police watchdog says cops' use of facial recog risks wrongful arrests
Policy, Legal & Compliance.context: Home Office figures released on Thursday to complement the report show similar positivity toward the technology among police officers, with only 4 percent reporting a negative...
Policy, Legal & Compliance.full_text: UK police forces must do more to prevent the wrongful arrests of people subjected to retrospective facial recognition (RFR) searches, according to a Criminal Justice Inspectorate that holds deep concerns about the way in which the technology is used. According to a report from His Majesty's Inspectorate of Constabulary and Fire & Rescue Services (HMICFRS), there is a large gap in understanding among police forces and the National Crime Agency about how RFR should be used in responsible policing. The inspectorate blamed "fragmented and underdeveloped" frameworks for governance and legislation. It pointed to a lack of bespoke legislation to provide a uniform approach to police facial recognition use – and said existing laws have not kept pace with the technology. HMICFRS also said the rules governing each force's use of RFR are mismatched, and called for a statutory code to be included in the forthcoming Police Reform Bill to set nationwide standards. Illustrating the breadth of misunderstanding across forces, the report noted that despite the message being routinely communicated by National Police Chiefs' Council (NPCC) reps, individual investigators "often" thought RFR results constituted evidence rather than intelligence. In many cases, they are unaware that RFR results require further enquiries before enforcement action can be taken. "We found that some investigators didn't always carry out enough corroborative enquiries before acting on potential matches," the report stated. "In a small number of cases, officers relied too heavily on RFR results, which led to inappropriate investigative action. "Although some forces had strengthened their processes after such incidents, practice remained inconsistent." Later in the report, the inspectorate described the findings as "deeply concerning." Some of the excuses police staff offered included acute demands on response teams leading to reduced opportunities to carry out further enquiries before acting on RFR matches. In one force, managers were known to encourage officers to "progress investigations quickly" after getting a match on the RFR system. However, the inspectorate clarified that just because an arrest is made, it does not necessarily mean it is wrongful, as investigators may need to rule out subjects from their inquiries. The onus for taking action should also be placed on the police forces themselves, given that some lack formal procedures regarding how RFR enquiries should be carried out, the report noted. The best forces had centralized facial recognition teams, which generally provided better governance and consistent processes. Officials fear long-term misuse of RFR, and other forms of facial recognition, will erode public trust in the technology, which it insists remains generally high. Surveys carried out in 2025 by the likes of the Ada Lovelace Institute and Alan Turing Institute, as well as the King's College London Policy Institute, showed a generally favorable view of facial recognition use in UK policing, with support ranging from 91 percent and 53 percent respectively. Home Office figures released on Thursday to complement the report show similar positivity toward the technology among police officers, with only 4 percent reporting a negative experience. The Register's comments section often paints a vastly different picture of public perception of facial recognition. Kathryn Stone, his majesty's inspector at HMICFRS, said facial recognition has transformed policing, allowing officers to compare images in seconds, allowing them to solve crimes more quickly, but echoed the report's main concerns. "Police forces must be able to show that appropriate safeguards are in place, risks relating to bias and data retention are effectively managed, and decisions are still subject to human judgment," she said. "A clearer statutory framework, stronger national standards and improved governance and oversight arrangements are essential to maintaining public confidence." As well as legislative and governance-related concerns, HMICFRS also noted in its report that officers' training around the use of RFR remains inconsistent, and if improvements were made, this would lead to more effective and lawful use of RFR across the UK. Another major issue was police forces' failure to meet their image retention obligations. Forces were found too often to retain custody images taken of suspects on the Police National Database, against which many RFR queries are made. Police guidance sets out the scenarios in which custody images can and cannot be retained, and the inspectorate found that forces have failed to delete images that should have been wiped. The Police Reform Bill includes a provision to group custody images with the likes of DNA and fingerprints, bringing about more robust measures to ensure they are retained or deleted in line with legal requirements. A Home Office review previously found in 2017 that introducing such a statutory framework was untenable. It concluded that police could not automate the deletion of these images, and doing so manually would be too time-consuming. Jasleen Chaggar, senior legal and policy officer at Big Brother Watch, said UK police cannot be allowed to continue to use RFR when it risks wrongfully arresting individuals. "The revelations that officers are treating facial recognition as bona fide evidence rather than a probability score is alarming," she said. "This approach significantly increases the risk that more innocent people will have officers knock on their door to arrest them for crimes committed in towns they've never visited, as we've seen before. "Worse still, police aren't even logging their use of retrospective facial recognition, meaning people could wrongfully become suspects in criminal investigations without any record of why they've been accused." Chaggar called on the government to "urgently step in" and help the UK's police forces to sort out the new frameworks needed for effective RFR use. ®

Policy, Legal & Compliance.title: Police arrest 354 suspects in dark web cybercrime crackdown
Policy, Legal & Compliance.context: "By leveraging complementary partnerships and surging resources across the U
Policy, Legal & Compliance.full_text:
Authorities arrested 354 suspects in a joint international operation targeting vendors and buyers on the Archetyp, Nemesis, Tor2Door, Bohemia, and Kingdom dark web marketplaces.

Codenamed 'Operation TorNado,' this law enforcement action ran from May 2025 to October 2026 and involved agencies from 14 countries.

"Additionally, law enforcement targeted vendors and buyers active on forums, single-vendor shops, and encrypted messaging services. National authorities conducted independent investigations with Europol's support, including cross-checks via SIENA and forensic analysis," Europol said.

"The operation highlighted the evolving resilience of dark web marketplaces, which continue to adapt despite takedowns."

They seized over €60 million ($66 million) in cash and cryptocurrency, 950 kilograms of illicit drugs (including amphetamines, cocaine, ketamine, psilocybin mushrooms, MDMA, and cannabis), and 57 firearms in Europe.

Law enforcement authorities also seized more than 4.8 metric tonnes of illicit drugs, 152 firearms, and over €150 million ($166 million) in the United States.

"Following the takedown of multiple darknet marketplaces and vendor targets in the previous JCODE operation, U.S. and international law enforcement agencies obtained intelligence to identify Dark Web drug traffickers, resulting in a series of complementary, but separate, law enforcement investigations," the US Department of Justice added.

"By leveraging complementary partnerships and surging resources across the U.S. government and Europol, Operation TorNado significantly disrupted the online opioid trade and sends a strong message that criminals operating on the Dark Web are not beyond the reach of law enforcement."

Operation TorNado follows several similar actions over the last six years, including DisrupTor in 2020 (which led to 179 arrests) and Dark Huntor in 2021 (in which 150 more high-volume darknet vendors were apprehended).

In April 2022, US authorities and German police also took down Hydra, the world's largest dark web marketplace at the time, with more than 19,000 seller accounts that were serving over 17 million customers worldwide.

One year later, in 2023, Operation SpecTor led to the arrest of 288 other suspects who allegedly sold illicit drugs on dark web markets and the seizure of €50.8 million ($55.9 million) in cash and cryptocurrency.

More recently, in May 2025, law enforcement also announced the arrest of another 270 dark web vendors and buyers from ten countries as part of Operation RapTor.

Policy, Legal & Compliance.title: FBI Says US Seized $1.2 Billion Worth of Cryptocurrency Stolen From Binance
Policy, Legal & Compliance.context: [ Read: North Korea Launches Missiles Toward the Sea to Protest Binance Hack Claims ] Also Thursday, the FBI blamed North Korea for a separate social engineering scheme that...
Policy, Legal & Compliance.full_text:
The FBI said Thursday that it had seized more than $1.2 billion of cryptocurrency reported stolen last month from Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange.

The theft of about $6.3 billion from Binance is regarded as the biggest crypto heist in history, and the FBI has previously attributed it to a North Korean hacking group known as TraderTraitor. The U.S. government and private sector have so far combined to freeze more than $2.7 billion of the stolen funds, and the Justice Department said Thursday that it has now obtained court authorization to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion of that total.

Typically in those situations, the U.S. government will file a claim of forfeiture with a judge, who will then determine who has a legitimate claim to the recovered funds.

[ Read: North Korea Launches Missiles Toward the Sea to Protest Binance Hack Claims ]

Also Thursday, the FBI blamed North Korea for a separate social engineering scheme that officials say resulted in the theft of $400 million worth of cryptocurrency over the last 18 months. That scheme, known as FaceStealer, involves a complicated chain of events combining the hijacking of popular messaging apps and the recording of deepfake videos.

U.S. officials have repeatedly accused North Korea of using cyber schemes to generate funds for its regime, including its illicit weapons program.

Policy, Legal & Compliance.title: Police dismantle Gootloader, CastleRAT, StealC malware infrastructure
Policy, Legal & Compliance.context: "Victim data will be made available via platforms HaveIBeenPwned, DIVD, CheckjeHack, NoMoreLeaks, Sekoia, The Shadowserver Foundation, and NL-NCSC, alerting victims of stolen...
Policy, Legal & Compliance.full_text:
Europol and law enforcement partners from nine countries have seized hundreds of servers and domains used by the Gootloader, CastleRAT, and StealC malware operations.

Gootloader is a malware loader active since 2020, StealC is an infostealer that helps exfiltrate credentials, cryptocurrency wallets, and other sensitive information from victims' devices, and CastleRAT is a remote access trojan that surfaced last year. All three malware families have been used by various cybercriminal operations, including ransomware gangs.

The joint action is part of Operation Endgame, an international law enforcement effort targeting cybercrime and "cybercrime-as-a-service" networks. This stage of Operation Endgame included law enforcement agencies from Bulgaria, Canada, Denmark, Germany, Moldova, the Netherlands, Poland, the United Kingdom, and the United States, with Europol and Eurojust coordinating the effort.

Together with private partners who helped identify, take down, seize, and block infrastructure tied to the three malware operations, the authorities seized 257 domains and 235 servers.

They also identified 6.4 million victim datasets on the targeted criminal infrastructure, stolen from malware-infected systems for use in other cyberattacks, including ransomware breaches.

"During the action, over 6 million victim credentials were identified in the criminal infrastructure owned by the cybercriminals and seized by the authorities during this week. The suspects were using these credentials, stolen from the victims after they infected them, to sell them and later be used for other cyber-attacks such as ransomware," Europol said.

"Victim data will be made available via platforms HaveIBeenPwned, DIVD, CheckjeHack, NoMoreLeaks, Sekoia, The Shadowserver Foundation, and NL-NCSC, alerting victims of stolen credentials caused by the CastleRAT malware. WordPress users are urged to update credentials, enable multi-factor authentication, and patch vulnerabilities."

Previous Operation Endgame actions

In June, as part of the same operation, law enforcement agencies also cleaned nearly 15,000 malware-infected WordPress websites and seized 106 servers used by the SocGholish botnet and the Evil Corp Russian cybercrime group.

Later that month, Operation Endgame disrupted malicious infrastructure used by the Amadey and StealC malware operations, taking down 326 servers and 142 domains and recovering around 27 million credentials stolen from more than 385,000 compromised systems.

One year ago, the same joint law enforcement action also took down over 1,000 servers used by the Rhadamanthys, VenomRAT, and Elysium botnet malware operations.

Previously, Operation Endgame targeted Smokeloader botnet customers and servers, ransomware infrastructure, the AVCheck site, and various other major malware operations, including DanaBot, IcedID, Pikabot, Trickbot, Smokeloader, Bumblebee, and SystemBC.
